Nov 5 (Reuters) - Investors embraced risk on Wednesday as a resounding victory for the Democrats in the US midterm electionsraised hopes of an end to the US-Iran conflict, driving an 8% slump in oil prices.

While Asian markets are likely to extend the positive trend on Thursday, tech-heavy indexes may lag amid concerns over tougher oversight of AI sector growth and data centres.

Australia's September trade data and Indonesia's Q3 GDP dominate a busy regional calendar. Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to hold rates steady at 2.75% as inflation remains contained. The Bank of Japan has just published its September meeting minutes and Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser is due to speak.

Wall Street and an index of global stocks surged as markets bet that legislative gridlock in Washington would minimise policy shocks. The Dow led gains and AI heavyweights such as Microsoft advanced but chipmakers and data centre operators slumped, with the Philadelphia semi-conductor index hitting a six-month low.

US crude futures closed 8.3% lower as the Democratic sweep increased hopes of an end to the Iran war. US Vice President JD Vance blamed the war for the Republicans' election losses.

The U.S. dollar eased and gold advanced on bets that curbs on government spending and AI expansion would cool inflation and shorten the Federal Reserve's tightening cycle.

Dow +3%, S&P 500 +1.6%, Nasdaq +1.4% as cyclical and defensive stocks rallied. Treasury yields fell with oil; 2yr -3bps to 4.581%, 10yr -6bps to 4.892% and 30yr -4bps to 5.28%.

The U.S. dollar index =USD shed 0.35%; EUR and CAD +0.35%, JPY +0.15%, CHF +0.5%, GBP +0.45% ahead of Thursday's Bank of England rate decision, AUD +0.55%, NZD +0.65% but CNH -0.1%. Bitcoin gained 4%.

Gold +3.4% and copper +0.1% after hitting a near 4-month low as tight supply offset AI concerns.

For more click on FXBUZ

(Krishna Kumar is a Reuters market analyst. The views expressed are his own. Editing by Sonali Desai)

(( krishna.k@thomsonreuters.com ))

Nov 04, 2026

Source

The Mexican Peso rallies against the US Dollar following the Democratic blue sweep in the US midterm elections, with Democrats set to control the US Senate and the House of Representatives starting in January 2027. Despite this, the lack of an agreement between the US and Iran could derail the emerging market currency and boost the Greenback. The USD/MXN trades at 18.59, down by over 1.29%.

USD/MXN retreats as US election risk fades, while Iran tensions and Banxico's upcoming rate decision pose fresh risks

The risks of US elections have passed, and the focus is on the Middle East. Recent newswires show that the course of negotiations between Washington and Tehran would be clearer on Friday, according to Al Jadeed, citing Arab diplomatic sources. In the meantime, the US Treasury issued fresh Iran-related sanctions, while US sources speaking with Al Jadeed said that the war enters a delicate phase ahead of the new US Congress taking office, in which the White House could opt for a resumption of attacks on Iran.

US economic data showed that business activity in the services sector, as measured by the ISM Services PMI, was below estimates, expanding at 54.5, down from 54.9 and below forecasts of 54.8. Some of the sub-components of the PMI declined, like the prices paid, but the employment index showed a modest recovery.

Other US data revealed that private companies hired more people than expected, according to the ADP Employment Change report, while the US trade deficit narrowed in September, with goods exports rising to a four-month high.

Ahead, the US docket will feature jobless claims figures on Thursday, followed by Friday's Nonfarm Payrolls report, which will update the status of the labour market in the US.

In Mexico, the docket was absent, but traders are eyeing the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) monetary policy decision on Thursday. The central bank is expected to hold rates unchanged at 6.50%, according to the latest survey and the futures market. The odds are 60% for a hold, while there's a 39% chance that Banxico could opt for a rate cut, revealed Prime Terminal.

Source: Prime Terminal

USD/MXN Price Forecast: Technical outlook

USD/MXN daily chart

In the daily chart, USD/MXN trades at 18.6012, keeping a clear bullish bias as spot consolidates well above the triple simple moving average cluster, whose latest reading stands near 17.8508. The pair also holds decisively over the former downward resistance trend line, now a distant reference around 14.7081, while the Relative Strength Index (14) at 56.53 has cooled from prior overbought extremes and now suggests steady but less aggressive upside momentum rather than exhaustion.

On the downside, immediate technical support is hinted by the triple simple moving average area at 17.85, which should act as the first cushion on any pullback, ahead of stronger horizontal demand at 16.89. Deeper retracements would likely find additional structural backing around the old trend-line break region near 14.71, though such a move would require a significant reversal from the current bullish configuration.

BOGOTA, Nov 4 (Reuters) - The technical team of Colombia's central bank on Wednesday cut its 2026 economic growth estimates to 2% from the previous 2.5%, and raised its inflation estimate for the year to 7.1% from the prior 6.9% estimate.

For 2027, the bank lowered its GDP growth estimate to 1.7% from the previous projection of 1.9%, and raised its inflation estimate to 4.8% from the earlier outlook of 4.3%.

(Reporting by Nelson Bocanegra, Editing by Daina Beth Solomon)

Fitch Ratifica Calificación de Axtel en 'A(mex)'; Perspectiva Se Revisa a Negativa desde Estable

Mexico Wed 04 Nov, 2026 - 2:03 PM ET

Fitch Ratings - Monterrey - 04 Nov 2026: Fitch Ratings afirmó las calificaciones internacionales de riesgo emisor (IDR; issuer default rating) de largo plazo en moneda extranjera y local de Axtel, S.A.B. de C.V. (Axtel) en 'BB'. Al mismo tiempo, afirmó la calificación nacional de largo plazo de Axtel en 'A(mex)'. La Perspectiva se revisó a Negativa desde Estable.

La Perspectiva Negativa refleja la opinión de Fitch de que la posible oferta pública de adquisición anunciada para las acciones de Axtel podría aumentar la concentración accionaria. También podría modificar la estrategia y el proceso de toma de decisiones de la compañía. Además genera incertidumbre sobre la futura política financiera de la compañía. Fitch dará seguimiento a la ejecución de estas posibles ofertas públicas en curso, que están sujetas a aprobaciones regulatorias.

El crecimiento sostenido del segmento empresarial de Axtel y una cartera de contratos sólida en las líneas de infraestructura y gobierno respaldan las calificaciones, que se ven atenuadas por la escala operativa menor de Axtel en comparación con operadores globales.

FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Posibles Ofertas Públicas en Curso: Las posibles ofertas públicas actuales generan incertidumbre sobre el futuro gobierno corporativo y la estrategia financiera de la compañía, lo que respalda la Perspectiva Negativa. 4 Tech Plus, S.A. de C.V. y Transtelco Holding, Inc. anunciaron posibles ofertas públicas de adquisición de acciones de Axtel. Las posibles ofertas podrían aumentar o modificar la concentración accionaria, generar incertidumbre sobre la futura estrategia empresarial y financiera de la compañía y potencialmente afectar su proceso de toma de decisiones.

Posicionamiento de Mercado: La evaluación de posicionamiento de mercado de Axtel de 'bb-' refleja su escala limitada y su entorno operativo (EO) competitivo. La compañía opera en mercados competitivos de telecomunicaciones y tecnología de la información (TI). Sus principales unidades de negocio tienen una participación de mercado limitada en sus mercados primarios. Axtel es el segundo mayor proveedor de México de servicios de telecomunicaciones fijas para empresas. Compite con Teléfonos de México, S.A.B. de C.V. (Telmex) [A- Perspectiva Estable], que mantiene una posición dominante en el mercado mexicano. La participación de mercado de Axtel es menor en servicios de TI. Sin embargo, su posición competitiva es más equilibrada porque el segmento está fragmentado.

Desempeño Operativo Adecuado: Fitch prevé un crecimiento de un dígito medio en 2027 y 2028. Los servicios tradicionales de voz continúan disminuyendo, pero los servicios de datos, principalmente por fibra, y las soluciones de ciberseguridad crecen rápidamente. La amplia gama de servicios de la compañía le permite atender la demanda creciente de largo plazo de estas soluciones en una industria competitiva. Fitch espera que el margen de EBITDA aumente a cerca de 30% en 2028 desde 26.4% en 2026. El caso base supone una mejora del margen entre 2026 y 2028 a medida que se disipe el efecto base de 2025.

También supone una mejora de la eficiencia de los costos de personal después de que la compañía incurra en costos de reestructuración a principios de 2026.

Desapalancamiento Gradual: Fitch espera que la deuda neta a EBITDA sea de aproximadamente 2.2x y que el flujo de cada operativo (FCO) menos capex entre deuda sea de aproximadamente 9.8% en 2026. Fitch espera que ambas métricas mejoren hasta 2028. El apalancamiento neto disminuiría a menos de 2x y el FCO menos capex entre deuda aumentaría a aproximadamente 20%. Los mayores márgenes de EBITDA y las menores amortizaciones de deuda respaldan la mejora hasta 2028.

Amplia Cobertura de Fibra Respalda la Diversificación Geográfica: Axtel tiene cobertura y capacidad de red adecuadas en México. Su red de fibra de 55,600 km se extiende por aproximadamente 77 ciudades e incluye cinco cruces fronterizos. Esto proporciona diversificación geográfica en todo el país.

ANÁLISIS DE PARES

El perfil de negocio de Axtel es similar al de Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Bogotá (ETB) [BB- Observación Negativa]. Ambas son proveedoras de servicios de línea fija de pequeña escala y tienen una diversificación limitada. Axtel tiene un perfil financiero más sólido. ETB tiene una flexibilidad financiera más débil y ha registrado demoras en refinanciamientos. ETB y Axtel tienen un apalancamiento neto similar, inferior a 2.5x.

Axtel opera en un mercado similar al de Total Play Telecomunicaciones, S.A.P.I. de C.V. (Total Play) [B Perspectiva Estable], pero tiene un perfil financiero más sólido. Las calificaciones de Axtel no están influenciadas por el Techo País de México [BBB+].

SUPUESTOS CLAVE DEL CASO DE CALIFICACIÓN DE FITCH

--ingresos de MXN12.5 mil millones en 2026, con un crecimiento posterior de un dígito medio, impulsado por los servicios de datos y ciberseguridad y por una cartera de contratos de infraestructura y gobierno;

--márgenes de EBITDA de alrededor de 26.4% en 2026, que se estabilizarán en aproximadamente 30% en 2028 y posteriormente;

--intensidad de capital de alrededor de 12.5%;

--distribuciones anuales a los accionistas a partir del mediano plazo, después de alcanzar un apalancamiento neto de 2x.

Insumos y Puntajes de la Herramienta de Calificación Corporativa

Fitch calificó al emisor de la siguiente manera, utilizando la Herramienta de Calificación Corporativa (CRT; Corporate Rating Tool) para obtener el perfil crediticio individual (PCI):

Los factores del perfil de negocio y financiero (evaluación, importancia relativa) son: gestión ('bb+', moderada), características del sector ('bbb', moderada), posición de mercado y competitiva ('bb-', alta), diversificación y calidad de activos ('bb', moderada), características operativas de la compañía ('bbb-', moderada), rentabilidad ('bb+', moderada), estructura financiera ('bbb+', baja) y flexibilidad financiera ('bb', moderada).

Los subfactores financieros cuantitativos se basan en los parámetros estándar del período financiero del CRT: 20% de ponderación para el último año histórico 2025, 40% para el año proyectado 2026 y 40% para el año proyectado 2027.

El PCI es 'bb'.

SENSIBILIDAD DE CALIFICACIÓN

Factores que Podrían, Individual o Colectivamente, Conducir a una Acción de Calificación Negativa/Baja

--un cambio sustancial en la estrategia financiera y empresarial después de la operación de oferta pública de adquisición de Axtel que afecte la calidad crediticia de la compañía;

--una contracción pronunciada de los márgenes de EBITDA;

--deuda total sobre EBITDA sostenida por encima de 3.5x o deuda neta sobre EBITDA sostenida por encima de 3x.

Factores que Podrían, Individual o Colectivamente, Conducir a una Acción de Calificación Positiva/Alza

--claridad sobre el resultado final de la operación, sin un efecto sustancial en la calidad crediticia de la compañía, podría estabilizar la calificación;

--una acción de calificación positiva requiere una mejora consistente en la escala del negocio y la diversificación;

--cobertura de intereses por EBITDA superior a 5x.

LIQUIDEZ

Axtel tenía efectivo y equivalentes disponibles de MXN786 millones al 30 de septiembre de 2026, frente a una deuda de corto plazo de MXN292 millones. La liquidez de Axtel está respaldada por un calendario de amortizaciones manejable, relaciones bancarias sólidas y un flujo de fondos libre (FFL) positivo. La deuda de Axtel continúa concentrada en préstamos bancarios, incluidos algunos de prestamistas internacionales.

PERFIL DEL EMISOR

Axtel es un proveedor mexicano de servicios de telecomunicaciones y TI para clientes corporativos y gubernamentales. Axtel es único entre las empresas de telecomunicaciones calificadas por Fitch en Latinoamérica, que tienden a obtener la mayor parte de sus ingresos de consumidores minoristas.

Las posibles ofertas podrían aumentar o modificar la concentración accionaria, generar incertidumbre sobre la futura estrategia empresarial y financiera de la compañía y potencialmente afectar su proceso de toma de decisiones.

Posicionamiento de Mercado: La evaluación de posicionamiento de mercado de Axtel de 'bb-' refleja su escala limitada y su entorno operativo (EO) competitivo. La compañía opera en mercados competitivos de telecomunicaciones y tecnología de la información (TI). Sus principales unidades de negocio tienen una participación de mercado limitada en sus mercados primarios. Axtel es el segundo mayor proveedor de México de servicios de telecomunicaciones fijas para empresas. Compite con Teléfonos de México, S.A.B. de C.V. (Telmex) [A- Perspectiva Estable], que mantiene una posición dominante en el mercado mexicano. La participación de mercado de Axtel es menor en servicios de TI. Sin embargo, su posición competitiva es más equilibrada porque el segmento está fragmentado.

Desempeño Operativo Adecuado: Fitch prevé un crecimiento de un dígito medio en 2027 y 2028. Los servicios tradicionales de voz continúan disminuyendo, pero los servicios de datos, principalmente por fibra, y las soluciones de ciberseguridad crecen rápidamente. La amplia gama de servicios de la compañía le permite atender la demanda creciente de largo plazo de estas soluciones en una industria competitiva. Fitch espera que el margen de EBITDA aumente a cerca de 30% en 2028 desde 26.4% en 2026. El caso base supone una mejora del margen entre 2026 y 2028 a medida que se disipe el efecto base de 2025.

También supone una mejora de la eficiencia de los costos de personal después de que la compañía incurra en costos de reestructuración a principios de 2026.

Desapalancamiento Gradual: Fitch espera que la deuda neta a EBITDA sea de aproximadamente 2.2x y que el flujo de cada operativo (FCO) menos capex entre deuda sea de aproximadamente 9.8% en 2026. Fitch espera que ambas métricas mejoren hasta 2028. El apalancamiento neto disminuiría a menos de 2x y el FCO menos capex entre deuda aumentaría a aproximadamente 20%. Los mayores márgenes de EBITDA y las menores amortizaciones de deuda respaldan la mejora hasta 2028.

Amplia Cobertura de Fibra Respalda la Diversificación Geográfica: Axtel tiene cobertura y capacidad de red adecuadas en México. Su red de fibra de 55,600 km se extiende por aproximadamente 77 ciudades e incluye cinco cruces fronterizos. Esto proporciona diversificación geográfica en todo el país.

ANÁLISIS DE PARES

El perfil de negocio de Axtel es similar al de Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Bogotá (ETB) [BB- Observación Negativa]. Ambas son proveedoras de servicios de línea fija de pequeña escala y tienen una diversificación limitada. Axtel tiene un perfil financiero más sólido. ETB tiene una flexibilidad financiera más débil y ha registrado demoras en refinanciamientos. ETB y Axtel tienen un apalancamiento neto similar, inferior a 2.5x.

Axtel opera en un mercado similar al de Total Play Telecomunicaciones, S.A.P.I. de C.V. (Total Play) [B Perspectiva Estable], pero tiene un perfil financiero más sólido. Las calificaciones de Axtel no están influenciadas por el Techo País de México [BBB+].

Fitch Asigna Calificación de 'AAA(mex)vra' a un Crédito del Estado de Campeche

Mexico Wed 04 Nov, 2026 - 2:58 PM ET

Fitch Ratings - Monterrey - 04 Nov 2026: Fitch Ratings asignó la calificación de 'AAA(mex)vra' al crédito BBVA 26 contratado por un monto de hasta MXN1,000 millones por el estado de Campeche con BBVA México, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero BBVA México (BBVA México).

La calificación de BBVA 26 se basa en la calidad crediticia del estado de Campeche [AA-(mex) Perspectiva Estable] y cuenta con factores clave de calificación que le permite una mejora potencial de hasta cuatro escalones por encima de la calificación de la entidad. Lo anterior es con base en la combinación de los atributos asignados por Fitch a los factores clave de calificación, de acuerdo con su "Metodología de Calificación de Financiamientos de Gobiernos Locales y Regionales en Países de Mercados Emergentes".

FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Desempeño de Activos - 'Rango Medio': Como activo fuente de pago, el crédito tiene afectado 5.1% del Fondo General de Participaciones (FGP) que recibe el estado de Campeche, lo que equivale a 6.71% de las participaciones excluyendo las que corresponden a los municipios. Para Fitch, el FGP cuenta con atributos de un activo valorado como 'Más Fuerte'. No obstante, dada la estrecha vinculación económica de Campeche con la actividad petrolera, la agencia ha observado volatilidad en la recepción de estos recursos, por lo que la valoración es 'Rango Medio'. La tasa media anual de crecimiento (TMAC) real del activo del período de análisis (2021-2025) fue de 5.4%, superior a la TMAC real del PIB nacional para el mismo período, de 2.2%. Debido a la caída en la recaudación federal participable (RFP), la agencia prevé una disminución en la recepción de participaciones federales para Campeche en 2026.

Fundamento Legal - 'Más Fuerte': Para la asignación de la calificación, Fitch se apoyó de un despacho legal externo de prestigio reconocido. La opinión sobre la documentación del financiamiento fue favorable; esta concluyó que dichos documentos contienen obligaciones válidas y exigibles al estado de acuerdo con el marco regulatorio.

Vehículo de Propósito Especial - 'Más Fuerte': La estructura del vehículo de propósito especial que se utiliza en el financiamiento es adecuada para satisfacer el servicio de la deuda (SD) y se considera un factor 'Más Fuerte'. Como mecanismo de pago, BBVA 26 está inscrito al Fideicomiso Irrevocable de Administración y Fuente de Pago No. F/0006, que Campeche formalizó en diciembre de 2010. El fiduciario es Banco Multiva, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero Multiva (Banco Multiva) [A+(mex) Perspectiva Estable], el cual para efectos administrativos lo identifica bajo el número E/006. Los recursos afectados como fuente de pago del crédito ingresarán al fideicomiso mediante depósitos directos de la Tesorería de la Federación (Tesofe), conforme se efectúen las ministraciones del FGP correspondientes a cada mes, de acuerdo con la instrucción irrevocable girada por el Estado de Campeche.

Riesgo de Tasa de Interés - 'Rango Medio': De acuerdo con el contrato del crédito, el estado podrá, pero no estará obligado a, contratar instrumentos derivados de cobertura o de intercambio de tasas de interés tipo CAP que, de ser el caso, serán pagados de manera directa por la entidad con recursos propios, ajenos al porcentaje de participaciones afectado. Campeche se encuentra en proceso de contratar una cobertura de tasa que cubra al menos 30% del financiamiento dispuesto, por un plazo de 36 meses. Fitch considera este atributo como 'Rango Medio' debido a que la mayor parte del financiamiento permanecerá expuesta a los riesgos de mercado y a la volatilidad de las tasas de interés.

Fondo de Reserva - 'Más Fuerte': Fitch considera que el fondo de reserva es sólido, reduce el riesgo de liquidez y la probabilidad de utilizarlo es baja, por lo que evalúa este atributo en 'Más Fuerte'. El crédito BBVA 26 tiene la obligación de constituir y mantener un fondo de reserva equivalente a 2x el SD (capital más intereses).

Razón de Cobertura de Servicio de Deuda - 'Más Fuerte': Fitch evalúa este atributo como 'Más Fuerte' debido a que las coberturas anuales del SD bajo el escenario de calificación se ubican por encima de 2x para BBVA 26, sin incluir el fondo de reserva. Este escenario incorpora las proyecciones de la agencia en cuanto al PIB nacional, su impacto en el activo afectado, así como la expectativa para las tasas de interés y la inflación en México.

DERIVACIÓN DE CALIFICACIÓN

La calificación del crédito cuenta con factores clave de calificación que permite una mejora potencial de hasta cuatro escalones por encima de la calificación del estado de Campeche [AA-(mex) Perspectiva Estable], como resultado de las mejoras crediticias con las que cuenta la estructura del financiamiento y de la combinación de los atributos asignados por Fitch, valorados en su mayoría como 'Más Fuerte'. Lo anterior es conforme a la "Metodología de Calificación de Financiamientos de Gobiernos Locales y Regionales en Países de Mercados Emergentes" de Fitch.

SUPUESTOS CLAVE

Los escenarios de calificación de Fitch son a lo largo del ciclo e incorporan una combinación de estreses en el crecimiento real del activo, tasas de interés e inflación, entre otras variables. Consideran la información histórica de dichas variables y las proyecciones mensuales de cobertura de SD naturales y con reserva del crédito hasta su fecha de vencimiento. Los supuestos clave para el escenario de calificación incluyen:

--activo: decrecimiento real del FGP de la entidad de 7.4% en 2026 y crecimiento real de 4.1% en 2027 y de 4.3% de 2028 a 2046;

--tasa de interés variable (TIIE de Fondeo compuesta por adelantado a 28 días): 7.1% en 2026, 7.6% en 2027 y creciente hasta 10.6% en 2046;

--sobretasa del financiamiento: margen aplicable conforme al contrato de crédito;

--inflación nacional: 4% en 2026, 3.8% en 2027 y 3.6% anual de 2028 a 2046. PERFIL DEL FINANCIAMIENTO

BBVA 26 se destinará a inversiones públicas productivas dentro del Programa Estatal de Infraestructura Carretera y del Programa Anual de Inversión Pública del Estado, tratándose en este último caso de proyectos sin fuente de financiamiento definida a cargo de la Secretaría de Salud y de la Secretaría de Desarrollo Agropecuario, conforme a lo previsto en el Decreto 184 mediante el cual la legislatura local aprobó el financiamiento. El crédito está denominado en pesos mexicanos, periodicidad mensual de pagos, perfil de amortización creciente, tasa de interés TIIE de Fondeo compuesta por adelantado a 28 días más un diferencial definido en el contrato de crédito de acuerdo con la calificación de la estructura y vencimiento en 2046.

Mexico Wed 04 Nov, 2026 - 2:58 PM ET

Fitch Ratings - Monterrey - 04 Nov 2026: Fitch Ratings asignó la calificación de 'AAA(mex)vra' al crédito BBVA 26 contratado por un monto de hasta MXN1,000 millones por el estado de Campeche con BBVA México, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero BBVA México (BBVA México).

La calificación de BBVA 26 se basa en la calidad crediticia del estado de Campeche [AA-(mex) Perspectiva Estable] y cuenta con factores clave de calificación que le permite una mejora potencial de hasta cuatro escalones por encima de la calificación de la entidad. Lo anterior es con base en la combinación de los atributos asignados por Fitch a los factores clave de calificación, de acuerdo con su "Metodología de Calificación de Financiamientos de Gobiernos Locales y Regionales en Países de Mercados Emergentes".

FACTORES CLAVE DE CALIFICACIÓN

Desempeño de Activos - 'Rango Medio': Como activo fuente de pago, el crédito tiene afectado 5.1% del Fondo General de Participaciones (FGP) que recibe el estado de Campeche, lo que equivale a 6.71% de las participaciones excluyendo las que corresponden a los municipios. Para Fitch, el FGP cuenta con atributos de un activo valorado como 'Más Fuerte'. No obstante, dada la estrecha vinculación económica de Campeche con la actividad petrolera, la agencia ha observado volatilidad en la recepción de estos recursos, por lo que la valoración es 'Rango Medio'. La tasa media anual de crecimiento (TMAC) real del activo del período de análisis (2021-2025) fue de 5.4%, superior a la TMAC real del PIB nacional para el mismo período, de 2.2%. Debido a la caída en la recaudación federal participable (RFP), la agencia prevé una disminución en la recepción de participaciones federales para Campeche en 2026.

Fundamento Legal - 'Más Fuerte': Para la asignación de la calificación, Fitch se apoyó de un despacho legal externo de prestigio reconocido. La opinión sobre la documentación del financiamiento fue favorable; esta concluyó que dichos documentos contienen obligaciones válidas y exigibles al estado de acuerdo con el marco regulatorio.

Vehículo de Propósito Especial - 'Más Fuerte': La estructura del vehículo de propósito especial que se utiliza en el financiamiento es adecuada para satisfacer el servicio de la deuda (SD) y se considera un factor 'Más Fuerte'. Como mecanismo de pago, BBVA 26 está inscrito al Fideicomiso Irrevocable de Administración y Fuente de Pago No. F/0006, que Campeche formalizó en diciembre de 2010. El fiduciario es Banco Multiva, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero Multiva (Banco Multiva) [A+(mex) Perspectiva Estable], el cual para efectos administrativos lo identifica bajo el número E/006. Los recursos afectados como fuente de pago del crédito ingresarán al fideicomiso mediante depósitos directos de la Tesorería de la Federación (Tesofe), conforme se efectúen las ministraciones del FGP correspondientes a cada mes, de acuerdo con la instrucción irrevocable girada por el Estado de Campeche.

Riesgo de Tasa de Interés - 'Rango Medio': De acuerdo con el contrato del crédito, el estado podrá, pero no estará obligado a, contratar instrumentos derivados de cobertura o de intercambio de tasas de interés tipo CAP que, de ser el caso, serán pagados de manera directa por la entidad con recursos propios, ajenos al porcentaje de participaciones afectado. Campeche se encuentra en proceso de contratar una cobertura de tasa que cubra al menos 30% del financiamiento dispuesto, por un plazo de 36 meses. Fitch considera este atributo como 'Rango Medio' debido a que la mayor parte del financiamiento permanecerá expuesta a los riesgos de mercado y a la volatilidad de las tasas de interés.

Fondo de Reserva - 'Más Fuerte': Fitch considera que el fondo de reserva es sólido, reduce el riesgo de liquidez y la probabilidad de utilizarlo es baja, por lo que evalúa este atributo en 'Más Fuerte'. El crédito BBVA 26 tiene la obligación de constituir y mantener un fondo de reserva equivalente a 2x el SD (capital más intereses).

Razón de Cobertura de Servicio de Deuda - 'Más Fuerte': Fitch evalúa este atributo como 'Más Fuerte' debido a que las coberturas anuales del SD bajo el escenario de calificación se ubican por encima de 2x para BBVA 26, sin incluir el fondo de reserva. Este escenario incorpora las proyecciones de la agencia en cuanto al PIB nacional, su impacto en el activo afectado, así como la expectativa para las tasas de interés y la inflación en México.

DERIVACIÓN DE CALIFICACIÓN

La calificación del crédito cuenta con factores clave de calificación que permite una mejora potencial de hasta cuatro escalones por encima de la calificación del estado de Campeche [AA-(mex) Perspectiva Estable], como resultado de las mejoras crediticias con las que cuenta la estructura del financiamiento y de la combinación de los atributos asignados por Fitch, valorados en su mayoría como 'Más Fuerte'. Lo anterior es conforme a la "Metodología de Calificación de Financiamientos de Gobiernos Locales y Regionales en Países de Mercados Emergentes" de Fitch.

SUPUESTOS CLAVE

Los escenarios de calificación de Fitch son a lo largo del ciclo e incorporan una combinación de estreses en el crecimiento real del activo, tasas de interés e inflación, entre otras variables. Consideran la información histórica de dichas variables y las proyecciones mensuales de cobertura de SD naturales y con reserva del crédito hasta su fecha de vencimiento. Los supuestos clave para el escenario de calificación incluyen:

--activo: decrecimiento real del FGP de la entidad de 7.4% en 2026 y crecimiento real de 4.1% en 2027 y de 4.3% de 2028 a 2046;

--tasa de interés variable (TIIE de Fondeo compuesta por adelantado a 28 días): 7.1% en 2026, 7.6% en 2027 y creciente hasta 10.6% en 2046;

--sobretasa del financiamiento: margen aplicable conforme al contrato de crédito;

--inflación nacional: 4% en 2026, 3.8% en 2027 y 3.6% anual de 2028 a 2046. PERFIL DEL FINANCIAMIENTO

BBVA 26 se destinará a inversiones públicas productivas dentro del Programa Estatal de Infraestructura Carretera y del Programa Anual de Inversión Pública del Estado, tratándose en este último caso de proyectos sin fuente de financiamiento definida a cargo de la Secretaría de Salud y de la Secretaría de Desarrollo Agropecuario, conforme a lo previsto en el Decreto 184 mediante el cual la legislatura local aprobó el financiamiento. El crédito está denominado en pesos mexicanos, periodicidad mensual de pagos, perfil de amortización creciente, tasa de interés TIIE de Fondeo compuesta por adelantado a 28 días más un diferencial definido en el contrato de crédito de acuerdo con la calificación de la estructura y vencimiento en 2046.

BOGOTÁ, 4 nov (Reuters) - El equipo técnico del Banco Central de Colombia revisó al alza su estimación de inflación para 2026 a un 7,1%, desde un 6,9% previo, reveló el miércoles el organismo en su informe trimestral.

Para 2027, el equipo técnico, cuyas consideraciones toma en cuenta la junta directiva del banco en sus decisiones de política monetaria, modificó su pronóstico de inflación a un 4,8%, desde un 4,3%.

Las proyecciones se ubican más lejos de la meta de inflación de largo plazo del banco emisor, de 3%, que no se cumple desde 2020.

Por otra parte, el equipo técnico revisó a la baja su estimación de crecimiento económico del país sudamericano para 2026 a un 2%, desde un 2,5% protectado antes.

Para 2027, el pronóstico de crecimiento económico fue revisado a un 1,7%, desde un 1,9%.

En su reunión de octubre, el banco mantuvo sin cambios su tasa de interés de referencia en 12,25%.

En lo corrido de 2026, la autoridad monetaria acumula un alza de 300 puntos base en su tasa de interés, con el fin de contener las presiones inflacionarias.

(Reporte de Nelson Bocanegra. Editado por Luis Jaime Acosta)

Recasts with comment from economists, context and more details from policy statement

  • Central bank keeps benchmark rate on hold
  • Committee votes unanimously for no change
  • Policymakers note inflation and slowdown risks
  • Statement stresses need for caution on next decisions

By Marcela Ayres

BRASILIA, Nov 4 (Reuters) - Brazil's central bank ended a run of interest rate cuts and kept borrowing costs on hold on Wednesday as it grappled with a worsening inflation outlook following President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection.

The central bank's rate-setting committee, Copom, unanimously voted to keep its benchmark Selic rate at 13.75% — one of the highest among the world's big emerging economies — having cut it steadily since March.

The decision had been expected by 33 of 48 economists polled by Reuters.

Policymakers raised their inflation forecasts, said price growth risks appeared tilted to the upside amid rising inflation expectations and dropped a reference to the likelihood of future rate cuts that had appeared in their previous statement.

They reiterated their pledge to keep monetary policy "adequately restrictive" to return inflation to target.

But they also highlighted a "more pronounced deceleration of domestic economic activity" and described the current level of their benchmark rate as "substantially contractionary."

The challenging outlook required "serenity and caution" with monetary policy, the statement added.

William Jackson, chief emerging markets economist at Capital Economics, said the committee had hinted that it might eventually resume the easing cycle. "But the government will need to take tangible steps to tighten fiscal policy and reduce inflation expectations," Jackson said.

LEAVING ITS OPTIONS OPEN

Former central bank director Fabio Kanczuk said the Copom had left its options open but he did not see a rate cut at its next meeting.

"That would require a very clear fiscal announcement from the government, and nothing like that is coming now. The plan is to stay on hold, see how fiscal policy evolves and how markets react."

Lula has yet to announce his plans for controlling public spending and his choices for finance minister and other key posts.

Sources close to the president said he is expected to reaffirm his commitment to fiscal discipline in a televised address on Sunday, though without outlining specific steps.

Wednesday's central bank decision follows a sharp fall in the value of Brazil's currency as well as the country's stock market after Lula's surprise turnaround victory over Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in an election runoff on October 25.

Immediately before the election, investors were largely pricing in two consecutive 25-basis-point rate cuts, one in November and another next month. On Wednesday they were expecting rates to remain on hold.

Between March and September, the central bank cut rates by a total of 125 basis points, although it stressed that borrowing costs needed to stay restrictive to bring down annual inflation, which is running at 4.6%, to the official 3% target.

Investors view the central bank's independence as key amid mounting fiscal uncertainty ahead of Lula's fourth term.

Some prominent members of Lula's left-wing Workers' Party have stepped up calls for lower official borrowing costs.

During his election campaign Lula pledged only gradual repairs of the public finances to deliver primary surpluses, without detailing how he would achieve them, and he made several promises for more public spending.

The Brazilian real BRBY last week posted its sharpest weekly loss since the 2008 global financial crisis. Borrowing costs in financial markets surged while stocks suffered their steepest weekly decline since the pandemic.

Economic growth expectations have shown a marked deterioration while analysts have raised their inflation and borrowing costs forecasts.

The central bank's policymakers raised their inflation forecast over the next 18 months to 3.5% from the 3.1% rate they saw in September.

Inflation projections for this year rose to 5.6% from 5.2% previously and for 2027 to 4.7% from 3.9%.

The worsening outlook compounds the pressure on Brazil's public finances. Gross debt is approaching 83% of gross domestic product while interest payments have climbed to roughly 9% of GDP over the past 12 months, among the highest debt burdens across the world's major emerging economies.

(Reporting by Marcela Ayres; additional reporting by Brendan O'Boyle
Editing by William Schomberg and Sanjeev Miglani)

(( marcela.ayres@thomsonreuters.com ; +55 11 5047-2444; ))

Se reproduce la columna del miércoles para otros suscriptores sin ningún cambio. Las opiniones aquí expresadas son las del autor, columnista de Reuters.

Por Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, 4 nov (Reuters) - La aplastante derrota sufrida por el Partido Republicano del presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump, en las elecciones de mitad de mandato (link) nos recuerda lo políticamente tóxica que es la inflación.

El expresidente Joe Biden aprendió esa lección hace dos años, y el martes le tocó el turno al Partido Republicano, mientras los demócratas se alzaban con una victoria «aplastante», haciéndose con el control tanto de la Cámara de Representantes como del Senado.

Trump se presentó a las elecciones de mitad de mandato con índices de aprobación personal y de confianza en su gestión económica cercanos a mínimos históricos, y gran parte de la atención se centró en su «mala gestión de la economía». Algunos indicadores de confianza de los consumidores a principios de este año se hundieron hasta sus niveles más bajos desde que se tienen registros, en la década de 1950.

En muchos sentidos, esto resultó sorprendente, por no decir desconcertante. La economía estadounidense presume de tener el crecimiento más rápido (link) entre los países del G7, con una expansión anualizada del 3,4 % en el tercer trimestre. El mercado bursátil alcanzó un máximo histórico (link) hace menos de un mes, y el patrimonio neto de los hogares es el más alto de la historia (link). Las solicitudes de prestaciones por desempleo se sitúan cerca de sus niveles más bajos desde la década de 1960 (link), y la tasa de desempleo es de apenas el 4,2 %, un nivel compatible con el «pleno empleo». (link)

Entonces, ¿qué llevó a los votantes a dejar todo eso de lado e infligir una de las derrotas más contundentes en unas elecciones de mitad de mandato a un presidente republicano en el cargo que se recuerde? En términos económicos, la inflación.

Lleva casi seis años por encima del objetivo, lo que ha agravado la presión sobre el bolsillo de los estadounidenses. A ojos de los votantes, las dos políticas más trascendentales y controvertidas de Trump —los aranceles del año pasado y la guerra con Irán de este año— convirtieron las dolorosas presiones sobre los precios en una crisis de asequibilidad paralizante.

Aunque el impacto inflacionista de los aranceles había comenzado a remitir al llegar 2026, los hogares se vieron entonces aún más afectados por una subida de los precios de la energía tras el estallido de la guerra con Irán el 28 de febrero. Los precios medios del gasóleo se dispararon hasta alcanzar un máximo histórico de más de 6,50 dólares por galón en septiembre, y la gasolina superó los 5 dólares por galón en junio, según datos de la AAA.

Los votantes estadounidenses suelen volverse en contra de los presidentes en el cargo en las elecciones de mitad de mandato, independientemente de su opinión sobre la economía. Las elecciones ofrecen la oportunidad de asestar un duro golpe al partido en el poder, dejándole claro cuál será la situación de cara a las elecciones presidenciales que se celebrarán dos años después.

Pero esta vez, ha sido un golpe de gracia.

INFLACIÓN FRENTE AL DESEMPLEO

Desde el histórico repunte inflacionista que siguió a la pandemia de COVID-19 y a la invasión rusa de Ucrania (link) en 2022, se ha venido gestando una crisis de asequibilidad a nivel nacional. Este fue un factor clave de los bajos índices de aprobación de Biden de cara a las elecciones presidenciales de 2024, que acabó perdiendo. La inflación es ahora más alta que en noviembre de 2024, y las preocupaciones por el coste de la vida se han disparado.

A diferencia del desempleo, la inflación afecta a todo el mundo, independientemente de su riqueza, sus ingresos o su estatus social. Las personas más pobres sufren de forma desproporcionada, ya que se ven obligadas a destinar una parte aún mayor de sus limitados recursos a necesidades básicas como la alimentación, la vivienda, el transporte y la energía. Además, si los precios suben más rápido que los ingresos, como ocurre actualmente, los trabajadores están sufriendo, en la práctica, una reducción salarial en términos reales.

Aunque una mayor inflación puede ser a veces el precio que hay que pagar por mantener una menor tasa de desempleo y un crecimiento económico más sólido, no todo el mundo lo ve así.

Un estudio de 2024 (link)realizado por Stefanie Stantcheva, de la Universidad de Harvard, señalaba que pocas personas reconocen las «asociaciones positivas o compensaciones» que conllevan los precios más altos. «Por el contrario, la inflación se asocia predominantemente con efectos económicos y sociales negativos, lo que la convierte en una prioridad para la acción política».

Los políticos en el poder deberían mostrarse muy cautelosos ante los largos períodos de precios elevados. Un artículo de 2019 (link) de los académicos Joseph Macri y Bahram Adrangi reveló que un aumento de un punto porcentual en el desempleo reducía en tres puntos porcentuales la probabilidad de que un presidente obtuviera una valoración positiva, mientras que un aumento de un punto porcentual en la inflación reducía en siete puntos porcentuales la probabilidad de obtener una valoración favorable.

Otros estudios llegan a la conclusión opuesta. Un artículo de 2022 (link), de Lina El-Jahel, Robert MacCulloch y Hamed Shafiee, reveló que un aumento de un punto porcentual en el desempleo es aproximadamente seis veces peor que un aumento de un punto porcentual en la inflación en términos del bienestar general de las personas, y hasta 13 veces peor en cuanto a su estado de ánimo negativo en el día a día.

By Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 4 (Reuters) - The crushing defeat suffered by US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections is a reminder of just how politically toxic inflation is.

Former President Joe Biden learned that lesson two years ago, and it was the Republican Party's turn on Tuesday, as the Democrats raced to a "clean sweep" victory, taking control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Trump went into the midterm elections with personal approval ratings and economic trustworthiness scores near record lows, with much of the focus on his “poor handling of the economy.” Some measures of consumer confidence earlier this year sank to their lowest levels since records began in the 1950s.

In many ways, this was surprising, if not baffling. The US economy boasts the fastest growth in the G7 group of nations, expanding at an annualized 3.4% pace in the third quarter. The stock market hit an all-time high less than a month ago, and household net wealth is the highest in history. Jobless benefit claims are near their lowest levels since the 1960s, and the unemployment rate is just 4.2%, a level consistent with "full employment."

So what made voters cast all that aside and inflict one of the most resounding midterm defeats on a sitting Republican president in living memory? In economic terms, inflation.

It has been above target for almost six years, compounding pressure on Americans' pocketbooks. In voters' eyes, Trump's two most consequential and controversial policies — last year's tariffs and this year's war with Iran — turned painful price pressures into a crippling affordability crisis.

While the inflationary impact of tariffs had begun to fade when 2026 rolled around, households were then hit even harder by a surge in energy prices following the outbreak of the Iran war on February 28. Average diesel prices soared to a record high of more than $6.50 per gallon in September, and gasoline topped $5 per gallon in June, according to AAA data.

US voters often turn against incumbent presidents in midterm elections, regardless of how they feel about the economy. The elections offer a chance to give the party in power a bloody nose, putting it on notice for the presidential election coming two years later.

But this time, it was a knockout punch.

INFLATION VS UNEMPLOYMENT

A nationwide affordability crisis has been rumbling since the historic inflationary burst that followed the COVID-19 pandemic and Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. It was a key driver of Biden's low approval ratings going into the 2024 presidential election, which he lost. Inflation is higher now than it was in November 2024, and cost-of-living concerns have snowballed.

Unlike unemployment, everybody is affected by inflation, regardless of wealth, income, or social status. Poorer people suffer disproportionately, as they are forced to spend an even greater share of their limited resources on essentials such as food, housing, transport and energy. Moreover, if prices are rising faster than earnings, as they are now, workers are effectively taking a wage cut in real terms.

While higher inflation can sometimes be the cost of maintaining lower unemployment and stronger economic growth, not everyone sees it that way.

A 2024 studyby Stefanie Stantcheva at Harvard University said few people recognize the "positive associations or trade-offs" of higher prices. "Instead, inflation is predominantly associated with negative economic and social effects, making it a high priority for policy action."

Incumbent politicians should be very wary of long periods of elevated prices. A 2019 paper by academics Joseph Macri and Bahram Adrangi found that a 1-percentage-point increase in unemployment reduced the probability of a president receiving a positive approval rating by 3 percentage points, while a 1-percentage-point increase in inflation reduced the probability of a favorable approval rating by 7 percentage points.

Other studies draw the opposite conclusion. A 2022 paper by Lina El-Jahel, Robert MacCulloch and Hamed Shafiee found that a 1-percentage-point rise in unemployment is around six times worse than a percentage-point rise in inflation in terms of people's general well-being, and up to 13 times worse in terms of their negative day-to-day mood.

David Blanchflower, a professor at Dartmouth College and a former Bank of England policymaker, has long argued that unemployment is more pernicious than inflation. He suggests that women, older people and the less educated are more concerned about unemployment, while younger and more educated people fear inflation more. His studies find that a one percentage point increase in unemployment reduces happiness by as much as six times more than a percentage point increase in inflation.

"In a nutshell, unemployment hurts more than inflation," he and his co-authors wrote in 2014.

In political terms, however, it would seem that US voters in 2026 disagree.

(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261104:nNRA2l.html_limpio: Grupo Financiero Banorte, el segundo mayor prestamista del país, confirmó que propondrá un pago extraordinario de dividendos a sus accionistas para fin de año, como ha estado evaluando desde el último trimestre. En una reunión programada para el 1 de diciembre, se votará sobre el monto del pago, que aún no se ha definido, pero que elevará el total de pagos del año al 70%. Marcos Martínez, CEO de Banorte, destacó que la generación orgánica de capital del grupo ha permitido esta posibilidad y que prefieren devolver el capital al mercado de manera segura y continua. El capital básico del grupo financiero aumentó del 12.56% al 13.20% entre el segundo y el tercer trimestre del año, superando el requisito regulatorio del 7%. Con esto, 2026 marcará el quinto año consecutivo en que Banorte proporciona un pago extraordinario a sus accionistas en la segunda mitad del período, elevando el total de pagos por encima del 50%. Rafael Arana de la Garza, CFO del grupo, agregó que están gestionando cuidadosamente la generación de capital para minimizar pérdidas inesperadas. Banorte también reafirmó su perspectiva anual, que implica un aumento del 8% al 11% para la cartera total, un margen de interés neto entre el 6.2% y el 6.5%, y ganancias que oscilan entre 62 mil millones y 64 mil millones de pesos, lo que representa un aumento del 5.5% al 8.9%.

São Paulo, November 4 (EFE) - The Central Bank of Brazil decided on Wednesday to halt its policy of interest rate cuts, maintaining the official rate at 13.75% per annum due to increased inflationary pressures and geopolitical tensions.

This marks the first time the central bank has opted to keep interest rates unchanged after five consecutive cuts, which began last March when the rate was at 15% per annum. EFE

The Monetary Policy Committee (Copom) of the Central Bank decided on Wednesday (4) to halt the cycle of interest rate cuts and maintain the Selic, the basic interest rate of the economy, at 13.75% per year. This marks the first meeting following President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) re-election. The decision was unanimous.

Copom had previously implemented five consecutive reductions of 0.25 percentage points in March, April, June, August, and September. In a statement, Central Bank directors noted that the measure aims to ensure price stability and "implies smoothing fluctuations in the level of economic activity and promoting full employment."

The deterioration in economic indicators' expectations was confirmed by the first Focus bulletin following the victory of Lula, released on Tuesday (3). According to the report, the estimate for the Selic rose from 13.25% to 13.50% per year by the end of 2026. Meanwhile, the forecast for the Broad National Consumer Price Index (IPCA), the official inflation indicator in Brazil, increased from 5.19% to 5.22% in 2026, exceeding the upper limit of the target of 4.5%.

One day after Lula's victory in the second round, the Ibovespa closed down 13.88%, at 176,608.23 points. In practical terms, R$ 734 billion evaporated from the market value of companies listed on the B3 in a single trading session.

The Central Bank emphasized that it "monitors with attention the unanchoring of inflation expectations for longer terms as this contributes to price determination and increases the cost of disinflation."

"The current context, characterized by a substantially contractionary Selic rate, significant increases in uncertainties surrounding the base scenario, higher inflation expectations, and a more pronounced slowdown of domestic economic activity, presents a challenging environment for monetary policy, necessitating calm and caution in its execution," stated Copom.

The Monetary Policy Committee (Copom) of the Central Bank decided on Wednesday (4) to halt the cycle of interest rate cuts and maintain the Selic, the basic interest rate of the economy, at 13.75% per year. This marks the first meeting following President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) re-election. The decision was unanimous.

Copom had previously implemented five consecutive reductions of 0.25 percentage points in March, April, June, August, and September. In a statement, Central Bank directors noted that the measure aims to ensure price stability and "implies smoothing fluctuations in the level of economic activity and promoting full employment."

The deterioration in economic indicators' expectations was confirmed by the first Focus bulletin following the victory of Lula, released on Tuesday (3). According to the report, the estimate for the Selic rose from 13.25% to 13.50% per year by the end of 2026. Meanwhile, the forecast for the Broad National Consumer Price Index (IPCA), the official inflation indicator in Brazil, increased from 5.19% to 5.22% in 2026, exceeding the upper limit of the target of 4.5%.

One day after Lula's victory in the second round, the Ibovespa closed down 13.88%, at 176,608.23 points. In practical terms, R$ 734 billion evaporated from the market value of companies listed on the B3 in a single trading session.

The Central Bank emphasized that it "monitors with attention the unanchoring of inflation expectations for longer terms as this contributes to price determination and increases the cost of disinflation."

"The current context, characterized by a substantially contractionary Selic rate, significant increases in uncertainties surrounding the base scenario, higher inflation expectations, and a more pronounced slowdown of domestic economic activity, presents a challenging environment for monetary policy, necessitating calm and caution in its execution," stated Copom.

Operadora de Sites Mexicanos, a telecommunications infrastructure company spun off from América Móvil better known as Telesites, will propose to its shareholders a merger with Sitios Latinoamérica (Sitios Latam), another infrastructure operator in southern Mexico that also emerged from the asset separation of the telecommunications giant founded by Carlos Slim.

The operation would allow Telesites to consolidate the assets of both companies to provide telecommunications infrastructure to mobile phone operators in Mexico and Latin America, the company stated in a press release.

"Operadora de Sites Mexicanos informs that, in the most recent session of the board of directors, it was decided, among other matters, to submit for consideration to the extraordinary general assembly of shareholders a possible merger between the issuing company and Sitios Latinoamérica, as well as to analyze the terms and conditions for its eventual implementation," the company added.

Both companies communicated that before holding their assembly, they expect to receive the necessary authorizations for this type of operation, as well as to comply with the other applicable legal conditions for the two companies.

The companies did not specify details about the merger, such as which entity might prevail and which might be dissolved; however, in terms of market value, Telesites (47.62 billion pesos) is larger than Sitios Latam (29.64 billion pesos), and is the first of the two to have been spun off from América Móvil. Similarly, Telesites was the first to exist.

Both companies have Gerardo Kuri Kauffman, one of the most high-profile executives within América Móvil's companies, as their CEO and a member of both boards of directors.

In 2022, América Móvil spun off part of its telecommunications tower infrastructure in Latin America to pave the way for the creation of Sitios Latam, which has a presence in Latin America, primarily in Brazil.

This move mirrored the one conducted six years earlier by the company founded by the Slim family with assets in Mexico, following a regulatory request that led to the establishment of Telesites, which was subsequently merged with Operadora de Sites Mexicanos (Opsimex). This entity holds América Móvil's infrastructure in Mexico and Costa Rica.

As of the end of 2025, Telesites had 24,660 sites in Mexico, in addition to 310 towers in Costa Rica. Meanwhile, Sitios Latam has over 38,300 towers across 15 countries, with América Móvil as its main tenant.

Shares of Telesites rose 0.8% on the Mexican Stock Exchange, while shares of Sitios Latam increased by 7%, on a day when América Móvil fell by 0.4% and the benchmark S&P/BMV IPC rose by 0.9%.

**Dassaev Rodríguez contributed to this report.

Telcel workers have formed the Mobile and Data Workers Union to confront layoffs and labor changes currently being implemented by the company. The movement seeks to establish its own representation in relation to the company's existing trade union. Benjamín Yair Ortiz Sánchez, the secretary general of the new organization, detailed that the union was initiated by workers from Customer Service Centers in section 9, which covers Mexico City, the State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos. The official registration of the union with the Federal Center for Conciliation and Labor Registration became effective on September 3.

Why did Telcel workers create a new union?

The new organization received guidance from Francisco Hernández Juárez, leader of the Mexican Telecommunications Union (STRM). "We are a union established in accordance with labor law that has the potential to represent workers from all regions of the country, not just region 9. With this, we aim to promote democracy and independence among trade union organizations," stated the union leader at a press conference. He explained that Telcel's collective labor agreement is currently under the control of the Union of Service, Communications and Transportation Workers of Mexico, a national industry union representing over 20,000 unionized workers. Benjamín Ortiz noted that the creation of the organization was motivated by internal labor changes within the company. For the past two years, Telcel has modified how it measures productivity, adjusted working hours, and implemented charges for mobile devices due to alleged prior administrative irregularities. These changes have led to a distancing from the primary union representation following the 2024 contract review. "We express our disagreement with commitments we consider unfulfilled. Additionally, we were excluded from the WhatsApp groups we had with the primary union, which we interpret as a form of censorship," the leader argued. Ortiz Sánchez emphasized that one of the most pressing issues for workers is the layoffs executed by Telcel. He cited the case of employee Marilú Pérez Flores Rodríguez, who was dismissed from her position. The primary union justified the dismissal, stating it was part of an agreement made with the company. If she did not accept the severance proposal, she would have to hire legal advisors herself to file a labor complaint, and if she proceeded, she risked harassment from the company, the union leader clarified.

The Mobile and Data Workers Union claimed to have recordings regarding the situation of dismissed workers and intends to request that labor authorities investigate whether the dismissals were unjustified terminations or reprisals for collective organization. The union reminded that Telcel is part of América Móvil, one of the telecommunications giants in Latin America. This context surrounds the layoffs of the subsidiary, as the company reported revenues of 90.295 billion pesos as of September this year and a net profit of 29.118 billion. "We must ask ourselves, if the company continues to grow and generate profits, why do workers still face layoffs and uncertainty about our labor future? Technological transformation is necessary and part of telecommunications, but it must be carried out with workers, not at their expense," demanded the leader of the new union.

Grupo Financiero Banorte, the second-largest lender in the country, confirmed that it will propose an extraordinary dividend payment to its shareholders for the year's end, as it has been evaluating since last quarter.

In a meeting scheduled for December 1, a vote will be held on the payment amount, which has not yet been defined, but it will raise the total payout for the entire year to 70%, the company announced during its third-quarter earnings call.

"The organic capital generation of the group has allowed us the possibility of an extraordinary dividend this quarter," said Marcos Martínez, CEO of Banorte, during the call. "We do not want to retain capital for ourselves; we would prefer to return it to the market in a safe and continuous manner."

The core capital of the financial group increased from 12.56% to 13.20% from the second to the third quarter of the year, compared to a regulatory requirement of 7%. The company stated that it is comfortable with levels between 12.5% and 13.5%.

With this, 2026 will mark the fifth consecutive year that Banorte provides its shareholders with an extraordinary payment in the second half of the period, pushing the total payout above 50%.

"We are carefully managing how the bank generates capital at a very fast pace because the discipline we have on the risk side keeps unexpected losses to a minimum," added Rafael Arana de la Garza, CFO of the group.

Banorte also reaffirmed its annual outlook, which implies a rise of between 8% and 11% for the total portfolio, a net interest margin of between 6.2% and 6.5%, and profits ranging from 62 billion to 64 billion pesos (an increase of between 5.5% and 8.9%).

Saltillo, Coahuila - Regarding the elections in the United States , including the gubernatorial election in Texas, which borders Coahuila, Governor Manolo Jiménez Salinas stated that regardless of the outcome, Mexico must continue building agreements with the government of the neighboring country .

On Tuesday, the midterm elections were held in the United States, during which all members of the House of Representatives, 35 out of 100 Senate seats, and 36 gubernatorial positions, including Texas , were elected. The Governor of Coahuila was asked for his opinion on the matter.

"We are very respectful of what happens in the elections of another country, and we believe that regardless of the outcome, Mexico must continue to build agreements with the United States for the benefit of both countries," Jiménez Salinas responded.

This election is particularly significant given the economic problems that have arisen in Mexico due to the tariff policies of Donald Trump . It is anticipated that, with a majority of Democrats winning, the American President will lose control in Congress, benefiting both our country and Coahuila.

"Both countries need each other; when we work together, we strengthen one another. I believe that regardless of what happens with the election, we must continue to consolidate the relationship," expressed the state governor.

It is worth mentioning that Manolo Jiménez maintains an excellent relationship with the current Republican Governor of Texas, Gregg Abbot , but the advantage he will have with the likely gubernatorial winner, Ginna Hinojosa , of the Democratic Party, is that she is of Latino descent, the daughter of a woman from San Luis Potosí .

After the results of the midterm elections in the United States, which represented a defeat for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party, the Latin American Confederation of Customs Brokers (Claa) considered that the situation regarding foreign trade with Mexico will remain largely the same, although some positive indirect effects may be experienced. In an interview with MILENIO, Claa president Fernando Ramos stated that U.S. trade policy will remain primarily under Trump's control, which is something he will not leave to anyone else. "The government policy of the sector will continue to be managed by Trump. That is his decision; it is part of his administration, and whatever he can continue to control, he will," the executive commented. Ramos pointed out that, as a result, he does not foresee drastic changes in trade decisions from the northern nation, particularly concerning the USMCA. "From the perspective of our sector, our businesses, and foreign trade, I really don't think things are going to change much. The trade policy is still being maintained by President Trump; right now we are still in the phase of seeing what will happen with the USMCA. It seems the negotiations will continue each year," he affirmed.

Following yesterday's midterm elections in the United States, the results revealed a majority victory for the Democratic Party, Trump's opposition, which will now control both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Claa President Fernando Ramos believed that the positive indirect effects for trade would involve Congress pressuring the president to end the war with Iran, thus potentially resulting in a decrease in oil prices. . . "We have seen how the war has increased the prices of gasoline and diesel for truckers; therefore, if there is a decrease, it would present an encouraging scenario for reduction," he indicated. . . The executive also asserted that another possible change could be a reduction in the crackdown on Mexican and other migrants, many of whom work in the transportation sector. "Now that all the border states are Democratic, there may be a decrease in pressure against migrants, who even with visas have faced this issue. For example, many truck drivers who hold B2 visas have had them revoked. This could positively impact their ability to work again, generating greater flow and higher profitability," he explained.

Washington, November 4 (EFE) - Shawn Fain, president of the United Auto Workers (UAW), stated on Wednesday that low wages in Mexico, as well as in China, are among the main trade issues facing the United States, while advocating for "strategic tariffs" to protect domestic companies.

In a press conference following the Democrats' victory in the legislative elections on Tuesday, Fain defended Mexican workers and blamed large corporations for exploiting wage differentials.

The union leader explained that "Canada is not the problem" because workers there receive fair wages and maintain a good standard of living.

However, he warned that the wage gaps with countries like Mexico and China, "where they pay poverty wages," are creating a race to the bottom in labor conditions that harms American workers.

"We don't want to punish workers in Mexico. We just want them to have a decent standard of living," Fain stated, adding that "the enemy is the greed" of large corporations that exploit wage disparities.

Fain highlighted that the UAW was one of the first unions to endorse newly elected Michigan Senator Abdul El-Sayed, who he said shares the union's position on tariffs.

He also noted that El-Sayed, who is a physician, has compared the implementation of tariffs to chemotherapy: it must be administered gradually so as not to harm the patient.

For this reason, the union leader supported the imposition of "strategic and selective tariffs," but criticized President Donald Trump's trade policy for imposing indiscriminate tariffs without a coherent industrial strategy.

Fain expressed hope that the Democrats, who will control both chambers of Congress starting in January, will reach agreements with Trump to "eliminate the stupid tariffs that make no sense" while maintaining those that protect American production.

He also criticized the political influence of billionaires, citing Elon Musk as an example, stating that he can contribute more than $400 million to elections and control space technologies capable of impacting conflicts like the war in Ukraine, which, in his view, demonstrates that the American system is profoundly unbalanced.

Democratic Party activist Isaiah Martin took to social media on Wednesday (November 4) to celebrate the victories of allies in the U.S. midterm elections and to thank Brazil for having "shown the way." In his post, Martin used the term "explode," referencing a comment made by federal deputy André Janones (Rede-MG) used on the channel "Exército do Lula." Follow Correio Braziliense on WhatsApp and receive the day's top news on your phone.

With the confirmation of a Democratic majority in the U.S. House and Senate, the activist expressed a desire to visit Brazil. "Alright, now that we've cooked those idiots, I want to visit Brazil," he posted. In another post, Isaiah reiterated a statement made the previous week and once again called for the deportation of Flávio Bolsonaro. . . By Beatriz Vasconcelos

After two days of not intervening in the foreign exchange market, the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (BCRA) resumed purchasing foreign currency this Wednesday. The monetary authority acquired USD 9 million, bringing gross international reserves close to USD 50.5 billion.

Since the beginning of the fourth stage of the monetary program in January 2026, the Central Bank has acquired USD 15.972 billion both inside and outside the foreign exchange market. This amount exceeds the annual target of USD 10 billion set in the agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) by more than 50%.

The official projection aims to close the year near USD 20 billion in purchases. The goal is to enhance the monetary authority's capacity to respond to potential currency tensions during 2027.

Interventions slowed down at the end of October. In the last eight sessions, the agency led by Santiago Bausili purchased foreign currency only three times. In fact, this Wednesday marked the first purchase of the current month.

In October, total purchases reached USD 1.395 billion, nearly triple the USD 473 million recorded in September, which was the month with the lowest level of official purchases so far in 2026.

During August, acquisitions totaled USD 768 million, following USD 2.162 billion in July. The monthly series also includes USD 1.418 billion in June, USD 2.596 billion in May, USD 2.769 billion in April, USD 1.671 billion in March, USD 1.557 billion in February, and USD 1.158 billion in January.

The recent upward movements of the real in Brazil following Inácio Lula Da Silva's victory in the presidential elections put pressure on the local foreign exchange market and forced the BCRA to pause its reserve purchasing policy to avoid adding tension to the exchange rate.

Despite this slowdown in buying activity, the BCRA's gross international reserves closed the session at USD 50.435 billion, having experienced a daily increase of USD 142 million. This improvement in the monetary authority's holdings is attributed to a 3.45% rise in the price of gold, which ended the day at USD 4,075.

Only surpassed by Mexico worldwide: the agricultural treasure of the Peruvian countryside that is setting historic records and already generating over US$ 1.34 billion abroad

Peruvian avocado exports reached US$1,342.8 million between January and August 2026, according to figures from the Ministry of Agrarian Development and Irrigation (Midagri) . This represents an 8.6% increase compared to the same period in 2025, establishing the country as the world's second-largest producer and exporter of this fruit, second only to Mexico .

During the first eight months of the year, shipments abroad totaled 719,425 tons, a volume 1.7% higher than the 707,118 tons exported during the same period in 2025. The increase in commercial value was also linked to an improvement in the average export price per ton, which rose from US$1,749 to US$1,866.

Peruvian avocado exports exceed US$1.340 billion between January and August 2026

The value of international sales of Peruvian avocados increased by approximately US$106 million compared to the first eight months of 2025. According to Midagri , this growth was accompanied by increases in various months of the analyzed period. In January, the year-on-year growth reached 57.3%, while in February it hit 50.6%.

  • The Lord of Miracles will tour Surquillo, Surco, and Miraflores before meeting with Pope Leo XIV in Las Palmas

June recorded the highest monthly export value, with US$247.3 million, marking a 10.8% increase over the same month of the previous year. In July, shipments maintained stable levels, and in August, they amounted to US$206.4 million, a figure 9.5% higher than in August 2025. These figures reflect the evolution of Peruvian sales during the 2026 campaign.

The Netherlands and Spain account for more than half of Peruvian avocado sales

The Netherlands emerged as the main destination for Peruvian avocados between January and August 2026. Exports to this market reached US$492.6 million, representing 36.7% of the total value sent abroad. Additionally, they recorded a 22.9% increase compared to the same period last year.

Spain ranked second among buyers, with purchases totaling US$266.5 million, which accounted for 19.8% of total exports and a year-on-year growth of 17.2%. Together, both countries comprised 56.5% of the value of Peruvian avocado sales. In terms of national production, La Libertad, Áncash, Lima, Lambayeque, Ica, Ayacucho, and Junín account for more than 80% of the fruit's output. Midagri attributed the increase in harvests to favorable rainfall conditions.

SECTION 1 CORPORATE PROFILE

1.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Mexico City, November 4 (EFE) - The Bank of Mexico (Banxico) will announce its penultimate monetary decision for 2026 this Thursday, amid widespread expectations that it will maintain its interest rate at 6.5%, due to warnings about inflationary and exchange rate risks, despite indications of openness from some members of its Board of Governors.

This decision follows the pause in September, when the central bank kept the reference rate at 6.5% in the context of inflationary pressures, exchange rate volatility, and differing monetary outlooks between Mexico and the United States.

Meanwhile, there is expected to be a divergence in the monetary discussion after the minutes from September revealed that three of the five Board members were open to considering new rate cuts.

According to the latest Citi Expectations Survey from the second half of October, 25 of the 37 analysts consulted anticipate that Banxico will keep its rate unchanged for the remainder of 2026 and all of 2027, while three expect movements this year and nine in the following year.

The median forecasts remain at 6.5% for both annual closures, although institutions such as Bankaool, Finamex, and UBS anticipate a 25 basis point cut this Thursday.

Similarly, Banxico's own October survey, released on Tuesday, placed the median expectation for the interbank funding rate at 6.5% at the end of 2026 and 2027, unchanged.

The survey, conducted among 40 analysis groups, slightly raised the forecast for overall inflation for 2026 from 3.87% to 3.88%, while the expectation for economic growth increased from 1.4% to 1.5%.

In its analysis, Bank of America expects Banxico to maintain the rate through a vote of four to one, although it acknowledges a significant probability of a rate cut.

On the other hand, Banamex warns of elevated risks regarding a new reduction, particularly due to the recent depreciation of the peso and international financial conditions.

The Mexican peso closed October at 18.8 units per dollar, reflecting a monthly depreciation of 4% and registering eight consecutive weeks of losses against the dollar, according to closing data from the Bank of Mexico.
