The population over 50 years old is gaining weight in the Colombian economy.

About 14 million people belong to this age group, with around 8 million surpassing the age of 60, according to figures from Dane.

Their capacity for consumption, savings, work, and entrepreneurship is driving a market that currently represents nearly 12% of the national Gross Domestic Product (GDP), with an estimated annual spending of $121 trillion.

This transformation has a name: the silver economy. It encompasses the set of economic activities related to the needs, capacities, and consumption habits of older adults, a segment that for years has been approached primarily through the lenses of health, pensions, and care, but is now also being viewed as an opportunity for businesses, entrepreneurs, and productive sectors.

The potential is not limited to the population currently over 50 years old. According to Dane's projections, by 2050 four out of ten Colombians will be that age or older. The demographic shift poses a challenge for institutions and the private sector which will need to adapt their products, services, and business models to a society that will live longer.

Carlos Alberto Sampedro Gaviria, director of the Center for Studies on Comprehensive Human Development at the University of La Sabana, noted in Nota Económica that longevity is changing the way sustainability is understood.

"We are learning to live longer faster than we are learning to organize society for longer lives," he stated.

For the academic, aging cannot be viewed solely as a cost for healthcare systems and insurance. A population that lives longer also consumes, works, saves, and engages in entrepreneurship for more years, which necessitates a reevaluation of the traditional structure of studying, working, and retiring.

In this perspective, the silver economy is not confined to serving older adults but also involves creating conditions for them to remain active, maintain their autonomy, and participate in society.

A Market That Opens Opportunities for Companies

Figures from the Silver Economy study in Colombia by Colpensiones illustrate the scale of this segment: people over 50 contribute about 12% of the GDP and generate an annual spending of $121 trillion. This volume of resources opens up possibilities for entrepreneurs who can identify the needs of a population that is not a homogeneous group.

A report from the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) titled "The Silver Economy: A Mapping of Actors and Trends in Latin America and the Caribbean" helps to identify the activities currently participating in this market.

Forty percent of the companies linked to the silver economy provide health and dependency care services. Another 21% are present in multiple sectors, while financial services account for 8% of the identified activities.

Consumer goods, tourism, and workforce-related services each represent 4.5%. Entertainment makes up 4%, while education and housing each represent 3%, and transport accounts for 1%.

The concentration on health and care reflects the immediate needs of an aging population. However, the diversity of activities shows that commercial potential also extends to tourism, housing, education, financial services, and entertainment solutions.

Opportunities can also begin to be identified before the age of 50. Adults aged 45 and older currently make up about 31% of the Colombian population, according to the cited Dane figures. Projections indicate this percentage will rise to 37% in 2033, 43% in 2043, and 49% in 2053.

This means that companies will not only need to respond to the needs of those who have already reached old age but also anticipate the expectations of those in earlier stages of life.

Health, Travel, and Autonomy: Priorities for the Silver Generation

Aging is also accompanied by changes in consumption priorities. A study by Target Insights and Data 8 found that 65% of individuals over 45 prioritize health care; 57% prefer leisure travel, and 44% want to spend more time with family.

The same analysis indicates that seven out of ten individuals in this segment are financially independent, reinforcing their importance as consumers and potential clients of new services.

According to XeniorStudio, the silver economy can also promote active aging through initiatives that encourage physical and mental health care from early stages, as well as productive uses of leisure time to keep older individuals active and healthy.

Housing is another area poised to gain prominence. In Spain, for instance, a significant portion of consumers in this market own fully paid properties and seek to remain in their homes as they age. This trend opens the door for housing solutions that facilitate autonomy, accessibility, and care without requiring people to leave their homes.

Saving is also a relevant factor. According to XeniorStudio, older adults typically have a greater capacity for savings compared to other population groups, especially those with higher educational levels, due to reduced financial commitments. This makes them an attractive audience for business models related to finance, wellness, and longevity planning.

Also see: Individuals under 35 represent nearly four out of ten loans granted in Colombia.

Digitalization, meanwhile, represents an opportunity that has not yet been fully realized. While there are persistent prejudices about the technological capabilities of older adults and a limited range of digital products designed specifically for them, more individuals aged 50 to 70 are using technological tools to manage their finances, communicate, and access entertainment.

The challenge for companies will be to understand that the silver generation does not conform to a single profile. Their needs vary based on income, assets, education, work activity, health conditions, and personal expectations.

The deficit of the United States in trade of goods with Mexico grew at an annual rate of 26.1% from January to September 2026, reaching a record of $184.019 billion, the Census Bureau reported on Wednesday.

The balance resulted from a 20.7% increase in U.S. imports of Mexican goods, amounting to $481.586 billion, and a 17.6% rise in U.S. exports to Mexico, totaling $297.567 billion.

The administration of President Donald Trump has declared that it is more concerned about the deficit the United States has with China than the one recorded with Mexico, but it has set reducing the overall trade deficit of U.S. goods with the world as one of its commercial priorities.

Specifically, the United States has increased its deficit with Mexico primarily due to rapid growth in its purchases of computer equipment, which contains a significant amount of Asian-sourced inputs, parts, and components. The Trump administration has not yet made any specific criticism regarding this.

The deficit with Mexico was the second largest for the United States in the first three quarters of the year, surpassed only by the negative balance with Vietnam ($190.928 billion, a year-on-year increase of 47.2%). Below this were deficits with Taiwan ($171.121 billion, +81.3%), China ($131.492 billion, -18.4%), and Thailand ($84.885 billion, +74.7%).

Broadly speaking, the U.S. trade deficit in goods is a result of low national savings relative to spending and investment, strong domestic consumption driven by the dollar as a global reserve currency, industrial outsourcing, and high demand for foreign consumer goods and inputs.

In its trade of goods with the world, from January to September 2026, the United States reported a deficit of $919.726 billion, a 6% decrease year-on-year. This figure originated from exports of $1.85 trillion and imports of $2.77 trillion.

The United States imports goods and services for various reasons: some cannot be produced domestically in sufficient volumes to meet local demand, or their production would be inefficient compared to other economic activities.

Furthermore, various products are supplied by foreign companies that can produce them at a lower cost or with greater efficiency. It is worth noting that due to the integration of global value chains, many of these imports contain components (such as semiconductors) or raw materials (such as cotton) sourced from abroad.

For various policymakers, the large trade deficit of the United States with China illustrates an inequitable relationship. In their view, this gap is a direct consequence of distorting policies, including trade barriers, state subsidies, and discriminatory regulations. In practice, certain Chinese products are characterized by quality and low prices.

At the same time, the Trump administration has maintained an aggressive tariff policy towards the world, with increased protectionism towards China. In its trade with this Asian country, U.S. exports totaled $83.517 billion, while imports reached $215.009 billion.

With Canada, U.S. imports amounted to $304.565 billion, while exports to its southern neighbor totaled $265.874 billion.

Marginally, Taiwan was the third largest supplier to the U.S. market, with sales of $215.332 billion, followed by China and Vietnam with $204.826 billion.

1.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 1 CORPORATE PROFILE

1.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

Por Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, 4 nov (Reuters) - (link)Los inversores pusieron su dinero a trabajar el miércoles, lanzándose a por acciones (link), bonos, divisas distintas del dólar y oro (link) tras las históricas elecciones de mitad de mandato en EEUU (link), en las que los demócratas consiguieron el control (link) de ambas cámaras del Congreso, arrebatándoselo al Partido Republicano del presidente Donald Trump . El optimismo generalizado también se vio impulsado por una fuerte caída (link) de los precios mundiales del petróleo.

En mi columna de hoy (link), analizo el papel que desempeñaron la elevada inflación y la crisis del costo de vida en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EEUU, que terminaron en una de las mayores derrotas de un presidente republicano en el cargo que se recuerdan.

Lecturas clave de hoy

  • La victoria arrolladora de los demócratas da un nuevo giro a las preocupaciones de los mercados sobre Irán, la IA y la deuda (link)

  • Las elecciones refuerzan las medidas de control de la Fed, pero persisten los riesgos para su independencia (link)

  • El déficit comercial de EEUU se reduce ligeramente en septiembre; las importaciones alcanzan un máximo histórico (link)

  • La subida de tasas del BCE parece casi segura tras el repunte de la inflación a su máximo en tres años (link)

  • Los bancos centrales mundiales se toman un respiro en octubre tras la oleada de subidas de septiembre (link)

  • Evolución clave de los mercados hoy

    • BOLSA: Japón -1,5 %, China (link) +2,3 %. Europa (link) +1,8 %, Reino Unido (link) +1 %. Brasil +1 %, rompe una racha de seis días de pérdidas. Nasdaq +1,4 %, S&P 500 +1,6 %, Dow +3 %.

    • SECTORES/ACCIONES: Nueve sectores del S&P 500 suben, dos bajan. Cinco sectores registran un alza del 3 % o más; el sector de consumo discrecional sube un 4,2 %. El sector energético cae un 4,8 %. Las acciones de los centros de datos y del sector de la defensa bajan. Las grandes empresas del sector sanitario registran ganancias de dos dígitos, pero CVS (link) cae un 12,5 %.

    • DIVISAS: El dólar (link) registra su nivel más bajo desde el 30 de septiembre. Repunte de las divisas emergentes, especialmente el peso mexicano y el chileno. El bitcoin sube un 3 % por encima de los 80.000 dólares.

By Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 4 (Reuters) - Investors put money to work on Wednesday, piling into stocks, bonds, non-dollar currencies and gold following historic US midterm elections that saw the Democrats win control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican Party. The widespread bullishness was also fueled by a steep fall in global oil prices.

In my column today, I look at the part high inflation and the affordability crisis played in the US midterm elections, which ended in one of the biggest defeats for an incumbent Republican president in living memory.

Today's Key Reads

  • Democratic sweep adds new twist to markets' Iran, AI, and debt worries

  • Election stiffens the Fed's guardrails, but independence risks remain

  • US trade deficit narrows slightly in September; imports hit record high

  • ECB rate hike looks nearly certain after inflation rises to three-year high

  • Global central banks hit pause in October after September hiking spree

  • Today's Key Market Moves

    • STOCKS: Japan -1.5%, China +2.3%. Europe +1.8%, UK +1%. Brazil +1%, snaps six-day losing streak. Nasdaq +1.4%, S&P 500 +1.6%, Dow +3%.

    • SECTORS/SHARES: Nine sectors on the S&P 500 rise, two fall. Five sectors +3% or more, consumer discretionaries +4.2%. Energy -4.8%. Data center, defense shares fall. Big healthcare stocks post double-digit gains, but CVS -12.5%.

    • FX: Dollar lowest since September 30. Emerging FX rallies, especially Mexican and Chilean pesos. Bitcoin +3% above $80,000.

    • BONDS: German bund yield lowest in two months, 30-year gilt yield posts biggest fall since May, 10-year yield lowest since July. US yields down 3-7 bps across the curve.

    • COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil tumbles, Brent, WTI -8%. Gold +3.5% back above $4,000/oz, best day since August 19.

Today's Talking Points:

Gridlock, schmidlock

Wait, aren't political gridlock and a "lame duck" president in Washington meant to be bad news for stock markets? Not if Wall Street's whoosh on Wednesday is anything to go by. As news of the Democrats' "clean sweep" hit the wires late on Tuesday night, Nasdaq futures were down as much as 2.5%. The tech-heavy index closed Wednesday up nearly 1.5%, and the Dow had its best day since April last year.

As it turns out, the certainty of knowing who controls what in Washington for the next two years is rather welcome. It offers a sense of predictability, and reduces the likelihood of more radical policies being implemented. If so, the political backdrop is calmer. Also, history shows market performance in the second year of a presidential term is often weak, so the bar for recovery after the midterms is low. Will this time be different?

Game-changer oil?

We're only at the midpoint of the week, but the plunge in oil prices on Wednesday puts Brent and WTI crude futures on course for their biggest weekly decline since the white heat of the global pandemic in April 2020. Brent is down nearly 20% so far this week, WTI is down 15%. This will cool inflationary pressures and, ceteris paribus, is bullish for stocks and bonds.

Trump admitted that the unpopularity of the Iran war was a major factor in his party's defeat. He also said this week that the US will stop its $4 billion annual funding of Israel after this year. Meanwhile, Qatar has stepped up mediation efforts to end the US-Iran conflict. Could an end to the war finally, this time, be in sight? The oil market is trading as if it is.

Take it to the Bank

The Bank of England decides interest rates on Thursday, and is expected to finally join most of its G10 peers in raising borrowing costs to combat inflation. It would be the Bank's first hike in more than three years. The UK already boasts the highest real rates in the G4, so a hike would widen that gap even further. Around 100 basis points of tightening is priced in by the end of next year, rates futures markets show.

Good news for sterling? Probably. The pound rose to a seven-week high against the dollar on Wednesday, and is close to testing $1.35. It is hovering around its highest level against the euro since March last year. FX strength will help cool inflation, but won't do much to narrow the trade deficit.

What could move markets tomorrow?

  • Germany industrial orders (September)

  • Euro zone producer price inflation (September)

  • Norway interest rate decision

  • Bank of England interest rate decision

  • Federal Reserve officials scheduled to speak include Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin

(Reporting by Jamie McGeever; Editing by Nia Williams)

Adds details from statement in paragraphs 3-4

BRASILIA, Nov 4 (Reuters) - Brazil's central bank on Wednesday ended a run of interest rates cuts that began in March and kept borrowing costs on hold as it faced the prospect of higher inflation following President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection.

The central bank's rate-setting committee, Copom, unanimously voted to keep its benchmark Selic rate at 13.75%, as expected by 33 of 48 economists polled by Reuters.

The statement offered little guidance on the central bank's next steps, with policymakers pledging to keep monetary policy "adequately restrictive" to return inflation to target.

Policymakers said inflation risks appeared tilted to the upside but they also noted the "more pronounced deceleration of domestic economic activity."

The challenging outlook required "serenity and caution" when deciding on how to proceed with monetary policy, the statement added.

The decision follows a sharp fall in the value of Brazil's currency as well as the country's stock market after Lula's surprise turnaround victory over senator Flavio Bolsonaro in an election runoff on October 25

Immediately before the election, investors were largely pricing in two consecutive 25-basis-point rate cuts, one in November and another next month.

In a sign of the shift in expectations caused by Lula's ballot box win, options contracts traded on Brazil's exchange earlier on Wednesday suggested investors were expecting rates to remain unchanged.

(Reporting by Marcela Ayres; additional reporting by Brendan O'Boyle
Editing by William Schomberg)

BRASILIA, 4 nov (Reuters) - El banco central de Brasil puso fin el miércoles a una serie de recortes de las tasas de interés que comenzó en marzo, y mantuvo los costos de endeudamiento sin cambios por la perspectiva de una mayor inflación tras la reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

El comité de política monetaria del banco central, conocido como Copom, votó por unanimidad a favor de mantener su tasa de referencia Selic en el 13,75%, tal como esperaban 33 de los 48 economistas encuestados por Reuters.

La decisión sigue a una fuerte caída del valor de la moneda brasileña, así como del mercado bursátil, después de la sorprendente victoria de Lula sobre el senador Flavio Bolsonaro en la segunda vuelta de las elecciones del 25 de octubre.

Antes de las elecciones, los inversores anticipaban dos recortes consecutivos de las tasas de interés de 25 puntos básicos, uno en noviembre y otro en diciembre.

(Reportaje de Marcela Ayres
Edición en español de Javier López de Lérida)

((Mesa de edición en español, santiago.desk@thomsonreuters.com ))

Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Record earnings provide a strong foundation, but the ability to manage the challenges posed by project delays and fluctuating market conditions will ultimately determine Southern Copper's growth and sustainability.

Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo Mexico, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

Oct 13, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Targets US$471 Million Investment at Toquepala

Southern Copper Corporation is poised to invest US$471 million in significant upgrades to enhance efficiency and ensure the operational continuity of its Toquepala mine in Peru. This investment is part of the company's broader strategy to bolster its mining operations in the region. The announcement was made on 14th October 2026, highlighting the company's commitment to maintaining productivity and sustainability in its mining activities.

The planned improvements will primarily focus on increasing the storage capacity of the Quebrada Honda tailings deposit, alongside enabling new operational areas. According to the modification plan submitted to the environmental certifier Senace, the tailings deposit elevation will be raised from 1,246.5 to 1,256.5 meters above sea level. This expansion will also involve enhancing the East waste dump capacity, augmenting auxiliary facilities in Concentrator Plant 2, and implementing a domestic wastewater treatment plant for the Villa Staff camp, among other critical actions.

The expansion of the East waste dump by 16.1 hectares is designed to facilitate the continuity of mining operations. By optimizing hauling logistics, the company aims to reduce the distance between mining phases and material disposal points, leading to greater operational efficiency. Furthermore, the core storage area has reached its maximum capacity, prompting the need for a specialized warehouse to ensure proper conditions for storage, access, security, and durability of geological information.

Most of the investment, amounting to US$396 million, will be allocated to raising the tailings dam, a key component of the operational upgrade. Southern Copper Corporation has also outlined a broader investment plan of US$8.2 billion in Peru through 2033, focusing on various copper projects, including Tia Maria and Michiquillay, as well as the expansion of the Ilo Smelter.

The Tia Maria project, with an estimated cost of US$1.8 billion, is currently under construction and is expected to produce 120,000 tons per year of copper cathodes. With approximately 50% progress, production is anticipated to commence between late 2027 and early 2028. Southern Copper estimates that Tia Maria could generate US$20.2 billion in exports and US$4.6 billion in taxes and royalties during its first two decades of operation, underscoring its potential as a vital source of fiscal revenue and foreign currency for Peru.

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

Oct 13, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Targets US$471 Million Investment at Toquepala

Southern Copper Corporation is poised to invest US$471 million in significant upgrades to enhance efficiency and ensure the operational continuity of its Toquepala mine in Peru. This investment is part of the company's broader strategy to bolster its mining operations in the region. The announcement was made on 14th October 2026, highlighting the company's commitment to maintaining productivity and sustainability in its mining activities.

The planned improvements will primarily focus on increasing the storage capacity of the Quebrada Honda tailings deposit, alongside enabling new operational areas. According to the modification plan submitted to the environmental certifier Senace, the tailings deposit elevation will be raised from 1,246.5 to 1,256.5 meters above sea level. This expansion will also involve enhancing the East waste dump capacity, augmenting auxiliary facilities in Concentrator Plant 2, and implementing a domestic wastewater treatment plant for the Villa Staff camp, among other critical actions.

The expansion of the East waste dump by 16.1 hectares is designed to facilitate the continuity of mining operations. By optimizing hauling logistics, the company aims to reduce the distance between mining phases and material disposal points, leading to greater operational efficiency. Furthermore, the core storage area has reached its maximum capacity, prompting the need for a specialized warehouse to ensure proper conditions for storage, access, security, and durability of geological information.

Most of the investment, amounting to US$396 million, will be allocated to raising the tailings dam, a key component of the operational upgrade. Southern Copper Corporation has also outlined a broader investment plan of US$8.2 billion in Peru through 2033, focusing on various copper projects, including Tia Maria and Michiquillay, as well as the expansion of the Ilo Smelter.

The Tia Maria project, with an estimated cost of US$1.8 billion, is currently under construction and is expected to produce 120,000 tons per year of copper cathodes. With approximately 50% progress, production is anticipated to commence between late 2027 and early 2028. Southern Copper estimates that Tia Maria could generate US$20.2 billion in exports and US$4.6 billion in taxes and royalties during its first two decades of operation, underscoring its potential as a vital source of fiscal revenue and foreign currency for Peru.

By Duncan Balsbaugh

November 4 (IFR)

• Hedge monetization fuels fleeting risk-on rally as oil plunge reverses yields
• Blue tsunami's AI slowdown threatens to crush tech earnings outlook
• The tactical bias is flat, looks to trade in the 5.05% to 4.80% 10s range
• Thurs Challenger job cuts, jobless claims, Productivity, three Fedspeakers

Treasuries initially came under renewed selling pressure (10s high 4.964%) following another round of surprisingly resilient economic data, with October ADP payrolls rising 86k versus 69k expected, while ISM services remained firmly in expansion territory at 54.5, with employment climbing to its strongest reading since February. Coming on the heels of yesterday's robust JOLTS report, the data provided a potentially formidable curtain-raiser for Friday's pivotal payrolls and wages, briefly returning the market's pricing of additional Fed hikes to a more traditional data-dependent footing. However, yields subsequently reversed lower, with 10s slipping back below 4.90% (4.883% local low) as crude plunged nearly 9% on the notion that the Republican election debacle, reinforced by JD Vance's criticism of the Iran war, would force Trump into a negotiated settlement. We think that conclusion is fundamentally misplaced. To the contrary, a politically weakened Trump may only embolden Iran and the Houthis to escalate guerrilla campaigns against Persian Gulf shipping and regional energy infrastructure, while trading partners become increasingly willing to challenge his tariffs. Moreover, we suspect the equity rebound was driven largely by the monetization of hedges on AI accumulated over the past week rather than any genuine improvement in the geopolitical or economic outlook.

Indeed, the Nasdaq 100's extraordinary round trip, from futures plunging 2.4% overnight to the index surging more than 2% intraday before closing up less than 1%, hardly inspires confidence in the durability of the post-election rally. Once those hedges are monetized, investors will be left substantially exposed to an increasingly vulnerable AI bubble, with stretched valuations, enormous debt-financed capital commitments and deteriorating earnings prospects now facing potentially formidable political and regulatory headwinds. The Democratic sweep, particularly in Texas, threatens to disrupt the hyperscaler data center buildout just as investors are beginning to question whether the extraordinary spending commitments can generate acceptable returns. Meanwhile, the newfound enthusiasm for "gridlock is good" looks destined for an exceptionally short shelf life. Trump's promise to work with Democrats was quickly followed by his "veto" message, while incoming House Oversight Chairman Robert Garcia's "lawyer up" warning offered a rather more realistic preview of the next two years. With investigations, subpoenas, and potential impeachment proceedings looming, as well as a government shutdown on December 11, we doubt Wall Street's beautiful bipartisan narrative survives even another week.

For Treasuries, we continue to view the 5.05% to 4.80% range in benchmark 10s as intact, with today's near 9% collapse in crude likely having exhausted itself near $87, where the 100- and 200-day moving averages converge to provide formidable technical support. A rebound in oil, particularly if Iran and the Houthis intensify attacks on shipping, would quickly undermine the market's newfound enthusiasm for lower energy prices and potentially return some upward pressure to yields. Accordingly, we would resist chasing the Treasury rally below 4.90%, preferring to wait for a move toward the formidable 4.81% Liberation Day resistance level to become tactical sellers, while remaining strategic buyers of duration at yields well above 5%, particularly toward 5.20% or higher should that opportunity reappear. More importantly, we suspect the combination of renewed geopolitical risk, tightening credit conditions, political paralysis and an increasingly fragile AI trade will ultimately overwhelm the narrative for multiple Fed hikes. Once the post-election hedge monetization has run its course, the market will still be left heavily exposed to the very risks it was hedging against in the first place, with the next bout of equity market disruption potentially unleashing another powerful flight to quality.

The tactical bias looks to trade in the 5.05% to 4.80% 10s range. Look for a 4.94% to 4.88% range in 10s.

Daily Economic Review for Wednesday https://www.ifre.com/economics/2508601/us-econ-daily-review-services-pmis-show-strength-adp-sees-another-solid-month-of-payroll-growth-in-october

Thursday's calendar includes a trio of data releases and a trio of Fed speakers. Data include the Challenger Job Cuts Report at 07:30, then weekly jobless claims and the preliminary Q3 Productivity and Costs report at 08:30. Fedspeak follows with FRB Cleveland President Hammack (voter, hawk) on stablecoins and safe haven currencies at 08:50, FRB Richmond President Barkin (nonvoter, centrist) on the economy at 09:10, and FRB Dallas President Logan (voter, hawkish) moderating a Q&A on AI and the workplace of the future at 19:00.

Treasury will announce 6-, 13-, and 26-week bills (e: $100/95/82bn) at 11:00, auction $115bn 4-week bills and $110bn 8-week bills at 11:30, and buy back up to $4bn in 1M–2Y coupons at 14:00.

Weekly jobless claims are expected to have remained very low by post-pandemic standards, even accounting for the demographic slowdown that has reduced job market churn. Consensus calls have initial claims for the October 31 week edging up 2k to 196k and continued claims for the October 24 week rising 9k to 1.710mn.

Productivity in Q3 is expected to have seen a strong gain, with the consensus being that it grew at a 2.8% annualized rate, twice as fast as in Q2. That would be consistent with the stronger than expected initial Q3 GDP print and impressive recent investment data. On the other side of the coin, unit labor costs are expected to have risen at a 0.6% rate, half the pace of Q2.

Colombian exports reached a value of US$541.7 million in September 2023, the highest recorded for that month since 2014, according to figures from Dane. This result was primarily driven by oil, reflecting a growth of 16.4% compared to September 2022.

The sales of oil and its derivatives played a crucial role in this performance, showing an annual increase of 4.2%.

Historical data indicate that the previous record for September was set in 2014, when external sales amounted to US$588.7 million. The 2023 figure exceeded that level by US$322 million, marking a 6.3% increase.

This result signifies a turning point in the evolution of exports for that month, after several years in which Colombia failed to recover the levels recorded in 2012, 2013, and 2014.

However, this record was not accompanied by uniform growth across all sectors within the export basket. The performance of fuels was decisive in achieving the result, while other categories experienced more modest advancements.

The group of fuels and products from the extractive industries recorded sales of US$2,236.5 million in the reference month of 2023, reflecting an annual growth of 13.3%. Within this grouping, oil and its derivatives were the most significant contributors.

Exports of oil, petroleum derivatives, and related products reached US$1,475.5 million, compared to US$1,152.5 million in September 2022. The annual variation was 4.2%, one of the largest increases among the main exported products.

In absolute terms, this category saw an additional US$423 million compared to the same month last year. This amount represented approximately 21.4 percentage points of the total exported in September 2023 and accounted for about 9.1% of the overall contribution to external sales.

However, the performance of other extractive products differed significantly. Exports of coal, coke, and briquettes reached US$546.7 million, with an annual growth of 1.5%, a considerably lower variation than that recorded by oil.

Meanwhile, sales of metal ores and metal waste fell by 6.4%, from US$363.5 million to US$143.8 million. In contrast, the category of other products reached US$7.5 million, with an increase of 269%.

This result highlights that growth in the extractive sector was primarily concentrated in oil and its derivatives. This composition raises questions about the sustainability of export momentum when a significant portion of the results depends on a market exposed to external factors.

In this context, geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran are relevant for analyzing the behavior of the international hydrocarbons market. Notably, in September, the average price of Brent crude was US$114 per barrel, according to the EIA, a price US$23 higher than the average recorded in August of the same year.

The price peaked at US$131 per barrel on September 15, following attacks on oil infrastructure and vessels in the region. The EIA attributed the increase to supply disruptions and the search for alternative shipments.

From the highs of 2014 to the recovery in 2023

The evolution of Colombian exports over the past 15 years shows a pattern characterized by significant fluctuations. In September 2012, external sales reached US$491.4 million, while in 2013 they totaled US$485.7 million.

The highest record was achieved in September 2014, when exports reached US$588.7 million. However, the landscape changed drastically over the following two years. In 2015, the value fell to US$287.3 million, and in 2016 it dropped to US$278.6 million, the lowest level in the entire series presented.

Starting in 2017, a gradual recovery began, with exports amounting to US$328.2 million, which continued to rise until reaching US$351.2 million in 2018. However, in 2019, exports fell again to US$379.8 million, and in 2020 decreased to US$253.1 million.

In 2021, external sales rebounded to US$379.2 million, and one year later reached US$477.8 million, approaching the levels recorded in 2014. Despite this progress, the figures still had not surpassed the peak achieved eight years earlier.

The trend shifted again in 2022, when September exports amounted to US$412.7 million. In 2023, they reached US$415.8 million, and in 2024 they hit US$462.1 million, not yet recovering the historical high for that month.

It was not until September 2023 that Colombia finally surpassed that record, achieving US$541.7 million. This figure not only surpassed the result from 2014, but also indicated a recovery in export value after several years of outcomes below the levels seen at the start of the previous decade.

However, this record was not accompanied by uniform growth across all sectors within the export basket. The performance of fuels was decisive in achieving the result, while other categories experienced more modest advancements.

The group of fuels and products from the extractive industries recorded sales of US$2,236.5 million in the reference month of 2023, reflecting an annual growth of 13.3%. Within this grouping, oil and its derivatives were the most significant contributors.

Exports of oil, petroleum derivatives, and related products reached US$1,475.5 million, compared to US$1,152.5 million in September 2022. The annual variation was 4.2%, one of the largest increases among the main exported products.

In absolute terms, this category saw an additional US$423 million compared to the same month last year. This amount represented approximately 21.4 percentage points of the total exported in September 2023 and accounted for about 9.1% of the overall contribution to external sales.

However, the performance of other extractive products differed significantly. Exports of coal, coke, and briquettes reached US$546.7 million, with an annual growth of 1.5%, a considerably lower variation than that recorded by oil.

Meanwhile, sales of metal ores and metal waste fell by 6.4%, from US$363.5 million to US$143.8 million. In contrast, the category of other products reached US$7.5 million, with an increase of 269%.

This result highlights that growth in the extractive sector was primarily concentrated in oil and its derivatives. This composition raises questions about the sustainability of export momentum when a significant portion of the results depends on a market exposed to external factors.

In this context, geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran are relevant for analyzing the behavior of the international hydrocarbons market. Notably, in September, the average price of Brent crude was US$114 per barrel, according to the EIA, a price US$23 higher than the average recorded in August of the same year.

The price peaked at US$131 per barrel on September 15, following attacks on oil infrastructure and vessels in the region. The EIA attributed the increase to supply disruptions and the search for alternative shipments.

From the highs of 2014 to the recovery in 2023

The evolution of Colombian exports over the past 15 years shows a pattern characterized by significant fluctuations. In September 2012, external sales reached US$491.4 million, while in 2013 they totaled US$485.7 million.

The highest record was achieved in September 2014, when exports reached US$588.7 million. However, the landscape changed drastically over the following two years. In 2015, the value fell to US$287.3 million, and in 2016 it dropped to US$278.6 million, the lowest level in the entire series presented.

Starting in 2017, a gradual recovery began, with exports amounting to US$328.2 million, which continued to rise until reaching US$351.2 million in 2018. However, in 2019, exports fell again to US$379.8 million, and in 2020 decreased to US$253.1 million.

In 2021, external sales rebounded to US$379.2 million, and one year later reached US$477.8 million, approaching the levels recorded in 2014. Despite this progress, the figures still had not surpassed the peak achieved eight years earlier.

The trend shifted again in 2022, when September exports amounted to US$412.7 million. In 2023, they reached US$415.8 million, and in 2024 they hit US$462.1 million, not yet recovering the historical high for that month.

It was not until September 2023 that Colombia finally surpassed that record, achieving US$541.7 million. This figure not only surpassed the result from 2014, but also indicated a recovery in export value after several years of outcomes below the levels seen at the start of the previous decade.

The continuity of the USMCA is secured following the Democratic Party's victory in the Congress and Senate of the United States.

BBVA Mexico is confident that there is no risk of a new trade agreement, as this decision would need to be voted on in Congress, which is no longer controlled by President Donald Trump.

"We believe the USMCA will remain in effect, and Mexico will continue to have a privileged position for exporting to the United States," said Carlos Serrano, chief economist at BBVA Mexico.

Currently, the agreement is valid until 2036. "We still have seven years during which President Trump will not be in office, and it can be extended, so we believe there will be a treaty for a long time," he asserted.

Following the Democratic Party's victory in states like Texas, where Mexico and the United States engage in significant trade, a more streamlined trade process is expected in that region.

"At times, there were measures that hindered the passage of trucks (through Texas), and I believe this will be expedited, so (the outcome) is good news," he said.

Voters punished rising food and energy prices at the polls due to the trade sanctions that the United States has imposed on various countries.

Although President Trump's narrative always included rhetoric about increasing tariffs, it is thought that the new Democratic majority will favor the continuation of the current tariff conditions and even a less aggressive policy.

Remittances to Mexico are expected to recover this year, with growth projected at up to 4.1% by 2027, according to forecasts by BBVA Research.

An analysis by the bank, in collaboration with the National Population Council (Conapo), estimated that next year the country will receive $66.7 billion in remittances.

For this year, BBVA estimates that Mexico will receive $64.1 billion in remittances, marking a 2.6% increase compared to 2025. This growth is notable following a 3.9% decline in remittances recorded in 2024.

After the elections in the United States, where the Democratic Party won control of Congress and the Senate, analysts expect this to help reduce the budget allocated to deportation policies.

"The budgets for these measures are going to decrease," said Gabriela Rodríguez, Secretary General of Conapo.

BBVA Mexico's Chief Economist, Carlos Serrano, stated that with less funding for ICE, there will be a better environment for workers in the United States, which, combined with a strong economy, will benefit money transfers.

Additionally, if the peso continues to depreciate against the dollar, Mexicans will likely take advantage of this to send more money, as this has been a common practice to stretch resources further.

"If we remain at similar exchange rate levels as the current ones, there should also be more remittances next year," he assured.

Regarding the remittance tax implemented by Trump this year, BBVA considered that while the measure could be reversed, it will not have a significant upward impact. A decrease in deportations is also expected following the recent election results.

The midterm elections in the United States have concluded. This process saw the entire House of Representatives, part of the Senate, and 36 governorships up for election. As projections indicated, the elections solidified a Democratic majority, which is crucial for the diplomatic relations between the administration of Abelardo de la Espriella and the government of Donald Trump.

The administration of De la Espriella has faced tensions with the Democratic Party, while simultaneously strengthening its alliance with the Trump administration...

De la Espriella's administration has recorded frictions with the Democratic Party, while also reinforcing its alliance with the Trump administration on geopolitical initiatives such as "The Shield of the Americas" and aligned stances on the Middle East and Israel. A couple of weeks before the elections, the Colombian president sparked controversy by publicly endorsing Republican candidate María Elvira Salazar. His position drew criticism from Democratic Congressman Gregory W. Meeks, the minority leader in the House Foreign Affairs Committee, who described the president's interference in Florida as "unacceptable," warning of a potential deterioration of the historical bipartisan approach with Colombia.

In response to these accusations, De la Espriella reaffirmed his commitment to the bipartisan nature of the relationship with the United States, emphasizing that "the support of both parties has allowed us to build a relationship that transcends governments and political differences."

This electoral outcome not only determined the control of the House of Representatives by the Trump administration but also put at risk the parliamentary ratification of various forms of assistance promised by the White House to Colombia. Although the House of Representatives lacks direct veto power over the president's foreign policy decisions, initiatives such as tariffs or the "Shield of the Americas" will continue their regional course. However, multi-billion-dollar packages, such as the $1 billion security assistance package, depend on the appropriations committees of Congress, which will be under Democratic control in both the House and the Senate.

You may be interested: Political world reacts to the approval of the submission law in Congress: What is missing?

In statements made to El Espectador , Congressman Meeks noted that during a direct dialogue with De la Espriella, he expressed his intention to "help and work with Colombia to ensure that a sufficient amount of those dollars reaches the affected areas," referring to the emergencies caused by the earthquake on August 10.

These legislative committees could also limit allocations for military equipment to the Colombian government, demand compliance clauses on human rights, or channel aid toward Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs). Despite the electoral landscape yielding an unfavorable outcome for the Trump administration — which endorsed De la Espriella during the Colombian presidential campaign — it is expected that strategic interest in the country will persist.

Recently, it was announced that U.S. Vice President JD Vance, along with senior officials such as Pete Hegseth (Secretary of Homeland Security) and General Dan Caine (Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff), will make an official visit to Colombia. The Colombian government plans to address the relief of current tariff rates during this meeting. In this regard, Trade Minister Mauricio Gómez Amín stated that advanced discussions are ongoing regarding tax reductions that will not depend on electoral outcomes.

Additionally, the agenda will prioritize U.S. assistance targeted at areas affected by the earthquake, focusing on departments such as Chocó, Valle del Cauca, Caldas, Risaralda, and Quindío. This scenario evokes a precedent for President De la Espriella, who has already experienced the electoral downfall of an ideological ally after openly supporting Flavio Bolsonaro against Luiz Inácio "Lula" da Silva in Brazil. On that occasion, similar to his stance with the U.S. legislature, he maintained that despite the "profound ideological differences," the bond between the two nations prevailed over any political circumstances.

The dollar experienced a significant decline this Wednesday in the Chilean foreign exchange market, dropping nearly $12 and closing the day at $969.9 for buyers and $970.2 for sellers . With this result, the U.S. currency broke below the $970 mark and reached its lowest exchange rate since mid-October, amid movements in international markets following the results of the elections in the United States .

Regarding the reasons behind this behavior, Patricio Ramírez , coordinator of the Economic and Social Observatory at the Faculty of Business Sciences and director of Commercial Engineering at the University of La Frontera (UFRO), explained that there are four main factors that pressured the exchange rate downward. Among them, he mentioned Donald Trump's legislative defeat, which weakened his ability to advance his economic agenda and created uncertainty among investors regarding the future direction of the U.S. economy.

This scenario was compounded by a decrease in the yield on U.S. Treasury bonds , which reduces the attractiveness of dollar-denominated assets and may encourage the search for alternatives in other markets. Additionally, the expert pointed to the international weakening of the U.S. dollar and the recovery in the price of copper, Chile's main export product, whose higher value boosts foreign currency inflow and strengthens the Chilean peso.

The drop in the dollar could also have favorable effects for both consumers and businesses. For individuals, a cheaper U.S. dollar could translate into lower prices for fuels and imported goods, more affordable foreign travel, and a reduction in inflationary pressures. For companies, it represents an opportunity to reduce costs associated with imports, production, and transportation.

However, Ramírez warned that this decline does not necessarily mean the dollar will maintain a downward trajectory . The economist noted that one should not confuse a market's temporary reaction with a permanent change in trend, as the evolution of the exchange rate will continue to be conditioned by the economic and political decisions Trump makes following the election results, the behavior of interest rates in the United States, and the performance of the global economy.

BUENOS AIRES, 4 nov (Reuters) - La ronda cambiaria de Argentina registró el miércoles su nuevo mínimo histórico para el peso doméstico ante una sigilosa recomposición de carteras en dólares frente a diversas presiones en danza.

Una economía que no despega, el riesgo de que el presidente libertario Javier Milei vea complicada su reelección y cierto atraso cambiario frente a altos costos dolarizados que perjudican a empresas, figuran entre las alarmas seguidas por los inversores.

Además, temas externos como el prolongado conflicto en Oriente Medio que impulsa al petróleo -con alza en la inflación-, y la caída electoral de la derecha en Brasil y ahora en las legislativas de Estados Unidos, también juegan en contra.

El peso mayorista anotó su piso récord en 1.565 por dólar ARS=RASL en la apertura con retroceso del 0,89%, para nivelarse luego hasta marcar una ligera mejora del 0,19% a 1.548 unidades al cierre con el seguimiento del banco central (BCRA), quien acumula casi 16.000 millones de dólares comprados en el año.

La autoridad monetaria volvió a la compra de divisas, luego de dos sesiones de inactividad, con un saldo favorable de apenas 9 millones de dólares.

"El mercado del peso está tranquilo, pero intentando cada día bajar algo más y así poder acompañar la devaluación de otras monedas en la región. Está claro que el Gobierno impide algún derrumbe fuerte por el temor a que se escapen las variables inflacionarias", explicó un agente del oficial Banco Nación.

El riesgo país de Argentina se movía en los 852 puntos básicos (2100 GMT), lo más alto en un año y tras duplicar su nivel en los últimos cuatro meses. Solo en octubre registró un salto de casi el 30%, lo que ha pegado en las paridades de los bonos públicos.

Milei es un aliado directo del mandatario estadounidense Donald Trump, por lo que la derrota republicana en las elecciones de medio término no es un buen indicio, lo que se suma a la reciente sorpresiva caída de Flávio Bolsonaro en las presidenciales de Brasil.

"El inminente bloqueo legislativo (en Estados Unidos) limitará de manera sustancial la capacidad de gasto público de la Casa Blanca, al tiempo que anticipan la implementación de un marco normativo más riguroso para la inteligencia artificial que podría moderar la expansión económica y disuadir a las autoridades monetarias de aplicar nuevos incrementos en las tasas de interés", comentó Wise Capital.

La bolsa porteña cedió un 2,28% al final de la rueda en su índice líder MSCI Merval .MMXMRVLGA, a contramano de la mayoría de sus similares regionales, y la deuda pública extrabursátil promedió un retroceso del 0,5%, con dinámica de negocios entre instrumentos de alto liquidez.

"No me extraña que los mercados (externos) reaccionaran bien con la mala elección de Trump (...) Durante el 2025 aumentó la incertidumbre internacional con la guerra comercial. Más incertidumbre mundial es menos movimientos de capitales, menos financiamiento de la demanda y menos crecimiento", remarcó Aldo Abram, director ejecutivo en la Fundación Libertad y Progreso.

"Desde las elecciones (locales) y hasta la guerra de Irán, a Argentina le entraban inversiones y crecía. Después salieron los ahorros de argentinos y extranjeros, desfinanciando la demanda interna y caímos en recesión. La suba del petróleo hizo aumentar nuevamente, fuerte, el riesgo internacional. Además, incrementó los índices de precios y llevó a la 'Fed' a subir las tasas", dijo.

El mercado argentino se apresta a una prolongada inactividad, comenzando este viernes sin bancos por el día del trabajador sectorial, pasando al lunes y martes venidero con cierre total de la plaza financiera dada la visita al país del Papa León XIV.

(Reporte de Jorge Otaola;
colaboración de Hernán Nessi;
Editado por Maximilian Heath)

Tue Oct 27, 2026: Southern Copper's Growth Prospects Clouded by Tia Maria Delays

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is navigating a complex landscape of robust earnings juxtaposed with project delays, particularly concerning its Tia Maria project in Peru. On the 27th of October 2026, the company reported record third-quarter revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and net earnings, enhanced by higher copper prices and strong contributions from its Mexican operations.

Despite these impressive figures, the company faces challenges due to falling copper prices and lower ore grades at its Peruvian mines. Southern Copper's production from its Toquepala and Cuajone mines has reportedly declined, necessitating increased output from its Mexican operations to maintain overall production levels. The delays at Tia Maria, where construction has been postponed to accommodate additional engineering work, add another layer of complexity to the company's growth outlook.

Southern Copper's successful quarter was largely driven by price increases rather than volume growth, raising concerns about the sustainability of such earnings in the face of fluctuating commodity prices. Management emphasized that while Mexican operations provided a necessary buffer, the ongoing issues in Peru must be addressed to ensure long-term stability. The company has a diverse asset base, operating across Mexico and Peru, but the current focus remains on overcoming the challenges posed by its Peruvian projects.

Looking ahead, the company has ambitious plans for growth, including a decade-long capital program aimed at increasing annual copper output. Projects like El Pilar in Mexico are set to advance, but uncertainties surrounding community relations, regulatory approvals, and production execution in Peru remain critical to Southern Copper's future performance. The market eagerly awaits updates on these initiatives, particularly the long-stalled Tia Maria project, which holds significant potential for enhancing the company's production capacity once operational.

Investors are advised to monitor Southern Copper's performance closely, as the interplay between copper prices, production volumes, and project timelines will play a pivotal role in shaping the company's trajectory. Mon Oct 26, 2026: Southern Copper Corporation Considers $968 Million Cuajone Expansion

Southern Copper Corporation is contemplating a significant expansion of its Cuajone copper mine in southern Peru, with a proposed investment of $968 million. The company announced on 28th October 2026 that the expansion would aim to increase milling capacity by 33%, from the current 90,000 tonnes per day to 120,000 tonnes per day.

Southern Copper's expansion plans would necessitate additional mining equipment and the establishment of a new production line at the Cuajone concentrator. The company estimates that the expanded operations could yield an average of 55,000 tonnes of copper and 1,400 tonnes of molybdenum annually, bolstering its output amidst current production challenges.

In addition to the immediate $968 million expansion plan, Southern Copper is exploring a larger scale enhancement that could increase milling capacity to 150,000 tonnes per day. CEO Raul Jacob indicated that while both options are under consideration, the 120,000-tonne-per-day scenario is currently deemed more feasible. A decision regarding the expansion's scale is expected in early 2027.

Despite these ambitious plans, Southern Copper has yet to finalize an investment decision or outline a specific construction timetable. The proposal comes at a time when the company faces challenges related to lower ore grades affecting its Peruvian operations, with mined copper production declining by 2.9% to 693,602 tonnes during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to diminished grades at its mines in the region.

Cuajone serves as an open-pit copper and molybdenum operation located in Peru's Moquegua region. Southern Copper Corporation, which operates several mines and metallurgical facilities in both Peru and Mexico, is primarily owned by Grupo México, holding an 88.9% stake in the company.

Por Manuel Farías

SANTIAGO, 4 nov (Reuters) - Las monedas latinoamericanas se apreciaron el miércoles frente al dóla, luego de que el Partido Demócrata logró un desempeño mejor al esperado en las elecciones de medio término en Estados Unidos, lo que generó alivio en los mercados emergentes.

* Los demócratas se hicieron el martes con el control del Senado y de la Cámara de Representantes, logrando victorias arrolladoras en bastiones republicanos por primera vez en generaciones, en una dura reprimenda de decenas de millones de votantes al presidente Donald Trump.

* La contundente victoria demócrata provocó la caída del dólar, al despejar una incertidumbre para los mercados que lidian con las repercusiones de la guerra en Irán y el auge de la inteligencia artificial, un fenómeno que ha impulsado tanto el crecimiento como la inflación, justo en un momento en que aumenta la carga de deuda de la mayor economía del mundo.

* "El dólar estadounidense sufre su mayor caída desde el 19 de agosto, luego de la victoria aplastante del partido Demócrata", dijo Banco Base en un reporte.

* Los demócratas obtuvieron "el control de ambas cámaras del Congreso, lo que limitará la capacidad del presidente Donald Trump para continuar impulsando su agenda económica durante los últimos dos años de su mandato", agregó.

* La fuerte caída de los precios del petróleo, presionados mientras los inversores aguardaban el próximo paso de Washington en el conflicto entre Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, limitó las ganancias de las monedas de los países exportadores de crudo de la región, como Colombia y México.

* Analistas señalaban que la atención de los inversores se mantenía también en las decisiones de política monetaria de los bancos centrales de la región. El Banco Central de Brasil publicará su decisión más tarde el miércoles y Banco de México el jueves.

* Las principales bolsas de la región acompañaron el optimismo, con avances liderados por Santiago y Sao Paulo.

* El peso mexicano MXN= subía por la tarde un 1,41%, a 18,5558 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice S&P/BMV IPC .MXX, integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, sumó un 0,6%, a 70.608,75 puntos, cediendo alzas previas que la llevaron a escalar casi un 2%.

* El peso chileno CLP=CLse apreció un 1,25%, a 970,20/970,50 unidades por dólar, su mayor nivel de cierre en más de un mes. El principal índice de la bolsa de Santiago, el IPSA, escaló un 2,52%, a 10.627,08 puntos.

* El real brasileño BRL= sumó un 0,64%, a 5,4511 unidades por dólar, al tiempo que el índice Bovespa .BVSP de la bolsa de Sao Paulo se empinaba un 1,06%, a 167.276 puntos en la última hora de negociaciones.

* El peso colombiano COP=RR cerró con alza de un 0,73% a 3.219 unidades por dólar, tras cinco sesiones consecutivas de pérdidas; mientras que el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP .COLCAPborró ganancias iniciales y terminó con caída de un 1,12% a 2.499,46 puntos.

* El peso mayorista argentino ARS=RASLganó un 0,19% a 1.548 unidades por dólar, tras anotar un mínimo récord en la apertura en 1.565 por dólar.

* En Perú, el sol PEN=PDSBse apreció un 0,46% a 3,4430/3,4460 unidades por dólar, y la Bolsa de Lima .MXNUAMPESCPGPE subía un 1,68%, a 1.495,41 puntos hacia el cierre de las operaciones.

(Reporte de Manuel Farías. Reporte adicional de Froilán Romero en Santiago; Nelson Bocanegra en Bogotá, Noé Torres en Ciudad de México, Hernán Nessi y Jorge Otaola en Buenos Aires. Editado por Javier Leira)

(( Froilan.romero@thomsonreuters.com ; Mesa de edición en español; santiago.desk@thomsonreuters.com ))

Acuña, Coahuila - Fire department personnel participated in the specialized railway safety workshop "TRANSCAER Piedras Negras-Nava 2026," organized by Ferromex and Grupo México , which took place in Piedras Negras.

The objective was to prepare first responders for potential railway accidents and leaks related to the transport of high-risk substances such as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), ammonium nitrate, and fuels.

Among the officers who attended the activities, held on October 3, were José Omar Llanas, Osvaldo Abimael Guerrero, Julio Felipe Macías, Francisco Javier García, Perseo Vázquez Medina, Edgar Martínez Santiago, and engineer José Andrés Reyes Molina.

The training involved support from a Ferromex tank car designed specifically for emergency simulations.

During the training, participants learned to identify hazardous materials on the railway network, use personal protective equipment, monitor hazardous atmospheres, and manage risks associated with LPG, as well as implement the Incident Command System.

The workshop brought together nearly 100 participants from the regions of Nava, Piedras Negras, Allende, and Acuña, as well as members of federal agencies, including the National Guard, and representatives from the Mexican Red Cross.

The training day would conclude with a general simulation.

Per Anders Nilsen, Norway's ambassador to Chile and Peru, highlighted to El Comercio the presence of Norwegian companies in our country, indicating that there are between 10 and 15 companies making investments in Peru. During the 'Norway-Peru Investment Forum 2026', he stated that a similar event is expected to take place in Oslo, the capital of the Nordic country, in November.

Trade cooperation, commercial interests, and investments are a very important agenda for us, because in Peru we have a group of Norwegian companies that are leaders in their sectors and are working in very strategic and important areas for Peru's development. This group consists of about 10 to 15 companies, some of which have been in the country for years and others that are exploring new opportunities.

Last year, we initiated an effort to bring these companies together with Peruvian actors and partners. It was a somewhat smaller format, but the response was incredible. We wanted to hold another forum this year, expand the format and our partners, and invite more players from both the Peruvian and Norwegian sides. This also comes months after a new government has taken office in Peru.

We believe it is a good opportunity to present the group, the commercial agenda, and the specific companies in the current context. It is truly a good starting point for developing our commercial agenda.

Creating this forum is a very positive sign, and Norwegian companies usually follow one another. I would like to mention another very important aspect: next month in Oslo, the Peruvian ambassador in Norway will organize a similar event in collaboration with the Oslo Chamber of Commerce.

We will also follow up on our part next year regarding Nordic cooperation. In April, we are starting the planning for a week of sustainable innovation together with the four Nordic embassies to celebrate Nordic-Peruvian cooperation on similar issues. We see a line of work, a plan, and a very positive agenda.

Over the last decade, we have witnessed very positive development. It is important to note that the relationship between Norway and Peru goes beyond trade and is evident in our companies: they are key players in their sectors, involved in renewable energy, agriculture, maritime services, port infrastructure, logistics, fishing, financial services, digital services, and human resources.

It is worth mentioning a global Norwegian company like Statkraft, which is significant in the production of renewable energy. It is currently building one of the highest solar parks in the world, at 4,500 meters. The company is also engaged in hydropower and other sources, producing around just over 4% of the energy in Peru, according to our estimates.

There are other examples: Kongsberg Discovery works with various partners in Peru, offering monitoring and digitalization services, which are vital for developing a sustainable fishing industry. I also mention DNV, which provides classification and sustainability standards. The Austral Group is a more established player in the country with a significant presence in the fishing industry. Odfjell Terminals is crucial for port operations in this country.

We are in sectors of the future that have great potential. Additionally, the largest private bank in Norway has many investments in Peru, and the Norwegian Global Pension Fund has around $400 million in investments in this country.

With Peru, we mainly export agro-industrial products, fruits, oils, vegetables, minerals, and animal fibers, including alpaca. From Norway, we export machinery, electrical equipment, technology, and specialized instruments. Currently, the trade balance is clearly in favor of Peru, which exports nearly 10 times more to Norway than vice versa.

With the EFTA agreement [whose members are Norway, Switzerland, Iceland, and Liechtenstein], a free trade agreement we have had for over a decade, Peru remains a fundamental instrument for trade and its potential.

It is a good agreement. In the current geopolitical context, this platform sends a message that Peru, Norway, and the other EFTA countries want free trade, clear rules, and predictability. We will see how far we can go in commercial growth, but both Peru and Norway have good products that deserve to be known and exported between us.

I was present for the change of presidency, and this is my return to the country in just a few months. It is an opportunity to meet the new government and have these conversations. I believe that the message from Norwegian companies truly reflects what they want in Peru and other countries: companies seek predictability, clear rules, and legal certainty.

I would like to point out a few important priorities for us. Firstly, political collaboration with Peru over several years and various governments, as we are two countries open to the world. I also emphasize our environmental cooperation, as we have been working for over a decade to halt deforestation in the Peruvian Amazon. We know that, with all the attention on the El Niño phenomenon, reducing tropical forest loss is one of the most effective measures to mitigate the negative impacts of climate change. There is an important agenda for us there.

Additionally, our cultural and friendship history spans many years: two countries rich in nature, living near the sea, with cultural interests, exploration, and indigenous peoples.

Press Release article 2 of 5, Source: WEC, 312 words

Dec 04, 2025: ASUR Calls for a Shareholders' Meeting

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V.(NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR) (ASUR), a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the United States, and Colombia, today announced the call to assembly for its General Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting which will be held on January 26 th, 2026 and announced the agenda for the meeting. The following is the complete text of the call to assembly for the shareholders' meeting: CALL TO ASSEMBLY FOR ORDINARY ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF GRUPO AEROPORTUARIO DEL SURESTE, S.A.B. DE C.V. By resolution of the Board of Directors adopted at the meeting held on the September 30th 2025 and pursuant to the provisions of Articles 36, 37 and other provisions of the bylaws of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (the "Company") and Articles 181 and 183 of the General Corporations Law ("Ley General de Sociedades Mercantiles"), the Company's shareholders are hereby called to attend the Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting (the "Meeting"), which will take place at 10 o'clock a.m. on the 26 th of January 2026, at the Company's offices at Bosque de Alisos No. 47-A 4 th floor, Colonia Bosque de las Lomas, 05120, Mexico City, Mexico, in order to discuss the following matters: A G E N D A I. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to acquire all or part of the shares and/or airport operators, including Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes, either directly or through its subsidiaries and/or special purpose vehicles. Resolutions thereon. II. Presentation, discussion and, if applicable, approval for the Company to, directly or indirectly, contract any type of debt, either through bank loans, securities issuances, or any other form of financing, and to enter into the contracts and agreements necessary and/or convenient to implement the foregoing.

Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Press Release article 4 of 5, Source: WEC, 182 words

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.
