Press Release article 3 of 5, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Nov 06, 2025: ASUR Announces Total Passenger Traffic for October 2025

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR), ASUR, a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the U.S. and Colombia, today announced that passenger traffic for October 2025 reached a total of 5.3 million passengers, representing an increase of 1.0% compared to October 2024. Passenger traffic increased 5.1% year-on-year in Colombia, while it presented declines of 0.2% in Mexico and 1.7% in Puerto Rico. Passenger traffic growth in Colombia was driven by increases of 14.8% in international traffic and 2.5% in domestic traffic. Mexico reported a 0.5% decrease in domestic traffic nearly offset by a 0.1% increase in international traffic. Puerto Rico reported an increase of 10.8% in international traffic more than offset by a decrease of 3.6% in domestic traffic. All figures in this statement reflect comparisons between the period from October 1 to 31, 2025 and from October 1 to 31, 2024. Figures excluded transit and general aviation passengers for Mexico and Colombia.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

Jun 09, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Publishes its 2025 Sustainability Report

GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 08, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces the publication of its2025 Sustainability Report, which presents the Companys performance, progress, and key initiatives related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters during 2025.

The report covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2025, and was prepared in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards and the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) framework. In addition, it incorporates considerations aligned with other international reporting frameworks, including IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2, issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB).

In February 2006, GAPs shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol PAC and on the Mexican Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol GAP. GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 05, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces preliminary terminal passenger traffic figures for May 2026, compared with May 2025.

Jun 09, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Publishes its 2025 Sustainability Report

GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 08, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces the publication of its2025 Sustainability Report, which presents the Companys performance, progress, and key initiatives related to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters during 2025.

The report covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2025, and was prepared in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards and the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) framework. In addition, it incorporates considerations aligned with other international reporting frameworks, including IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards S1 and S2, issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB).

The full report is available on GAPs website at www.aeropuertosgap.com.mx under the Investors section.

Company Description

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) operates 12 airports throughout Mexicos Pacific region, including the major cities of Guadalajara and Tijuana, the four tourist destinations of Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos, La Paz and Manzanillo, and six other mid-sized cities: Hermosillo, Guanajuato, Morelia, Aguascalientes, Mexicali, and Los Mochis. In February 2006, GAPs shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol PAC and on the Mexican Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol GAP. In April 2015, GAP acquired 100% of Desarrollo de Concessioner Aeroportuarias, S.L., which owns a majority stake in MBJ Airports Limited, a company operating Sangster International Airport in Montego Bay, Jamaica. In October 2018, GAP entered into a concession agreement for the Norman Manley International Airport operation in Kingston, Jamaica, and took control of the operation in October 2019.

In accordance with Section 806 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 and Article 42 of the Ley del Mercado de Valores, GAP has implemented a whistleblower program, which allows complainants to anonymously and confidentially report suspected activities that involve criminal conduct or violations.

Jun 05, 2026: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Reports a Passenger Traffic Decrease in May 2026 of 4.1% Compared to 2025

GUADALAJARA, Mexico, June 05, 2026 -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico, S.A.B. de C.V., (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the Company or GAP) announces preliminary terminal passenger traffic figures for May 2026, compared with May 2025.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) has successfully finalized its acquisition of Cross Border Xpress, marking a significant milestone in its expansion strategy. By bypassing traditional border crossing queues, the high-traffic facility generates significant revenue, further complementing Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico's existing airport operations in Tijuana. As a leading airport operator, GAP manages 12 airports across Mexico's Pacific region, serving multiple cities and popular tourist destinations. This acquisition aligns with GAP's strategy to bolster its position in the aviation sector.

In addition to its core aeronautical services, Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico diversifies its revenue streams through non-aeronautical activities, which include commercial services such as car parking, shops, hotels, and restaurants. The acquisition of Cross Border Xpress is expected to enhance these non-aeronautical revenue opportunities, with potential expansions in food and beverage services and VIP lounges anticipated.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Solvency of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.36; a deterioration from 0.35 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.18; steady from 0.18 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Altman-Z score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de scores a Z = 1.23 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]; a deterioration from 1.24 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Beneish M-score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

The Beneish M-score is calculated by using 8 key metrics:

Days Sales in Receivables Index

Gross Margin Index

Asset Quality Index

Sales Growth Index

Depreciation Index

Sales General and Administrative Expenses Index

Leverage Index

Total Accruals to Total Assets Index

Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de has a Beneish M-Score of -4.77 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]. An M-score of less than -1.78 is considered normal. However an M-score greater than -1.78 suggests there could be modifications to its earnings that have occurred to help window dress the headline earnings. Currently about 16 International Depository Receipts companies have a Beneish M-score greater than -1.78.

Piotroski F-Score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 5 for the half year-ended 30 June 2025 indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite one data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de scores an O = -9.845

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

The major supermarkets listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV), such as Walmart, Chedraui, and La Comer, experienced total revenue growth in the Mexican market during the third quarter of the year, a different situation from that of Organización Soriana. Despite these results, analysts and the companies themselves emphasize that consumer behavior remains cautious.

Specifically, Walmart de México increased its total revenue in the country by 3.1%, while Grupo Comercial Chedraui and La Comer saw increases of 4.6% each in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the same period a year earlier in the Mexican market.

On the other hand, Soriana reported a 4.3% decline in its revenue from July to September of this year, compared to the same period a year prior, according to its financial report.

Walmart sees cautious consumers

Cristian Barrientos, president and CEO of Walmart de México y Centroamérica, mentioned in a previous quarterly call with analysts that they are observing consumers becoming more cautious.

Amid this scenario, the company launched a campaign called "Prices That Cannot Be Touched" in the country , featuring over 4,000 items at fixed prices for more than 90 days.

Walmart de México reported modest growth in revenue, which has come amidst operational pressures due to its strategy of prioritizing market share and store openings. However, the slowdown in consumption and investments in pricing, logistics, and digital capabilities continue to limit short-term operational leverage," added Ariel Méndez, an analyst at Ve por Más, in a report.

Regarding La Comer, the analyst noted that although net revenue continues to grow above inflation, pressures from rising costs and expenses are eroding margins and the company's net profitability.

Weakness in Southern Mexico: Chedraui

Meanwhile, Chedraui has been affected by weak performance in Southern Mexico, a region that accounts for approximately 42% of its net sales .

This effect has significantly impacted our overall growth... The region is still suffering from tourism issues. I believe that the sargassum crisis, the dollar-peso exchange rate, and security concerns have undoubtedly affected that particular region," stated José Antonio Chedraui, the company's director, during a conference with analysts and investors regarding the company's quarterly financial results.

Nonetheless, the executive from the retailer originally from Xalapa, Veracruz, is confident that this is a cyclical issue and that they will be able to recover in the region .

Walmart and La Comer report comparable sales increases

In terms of same-store sales , which pertain to units operating for over a year, Walmart de México and La Comer recorded increases of 1.7% and 1%, respectively, from July to September of this year compared to the same period in 2025.

In contrast, Soriana and Chedraui in Mexico reported a decrease of 3.26% and 0.7%, respectively, in their comparable sales for the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same timeframe a year earlier.

As the year comes to a close, supermarkets may see positive results due to a mix of various factors such as El Buen Fin, year-end celebrations, and advance purchases for the Three Kings Day. The indicators that will influence sales at these stores will also be determined by formal employment levels and the inflation rate at the close of 2026.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

5.1 Activities

Kimberly-Clark de Mexico S.A. de C.V., a subsidiary of the global Kimberly-Clark Corporation, is a leading manufacturer and marketer of personal care and consumer tissue products in Mexico. The company specializes in producing a diverse portfolio of essential items, including baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, facial tissues, toilet paper, and professional wipes for healthcare and industrial applications. Its operations emphasize innovation, sustainability, and efficient supply chain management to serve both domestic and international markets. Among its fastest-growing segments are premium personal care products, such as advanced incontinence and feminine care solutions, fueled by rising consumer demand for high-quality, eco-friendly options and expanding e-commerce channels. Additionally, the professional segment, particularly wipes and protective gear, has seen strong growth due to increased adoption in healthcare and workplace safety sectors, positioning the company for continued market expansion in Latin America. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 19th largest Health care company by market capitalization.

PHOENIX, Tuesday, November 03 2026 - Ahead of this morning's market opening, Southern Copper Corporation closed lower the previous trading day. Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO), the NYSE's largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market cap, fell 2.2% during its previous trading session to close at $173.49.

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, renowned for its extensive copper mining operations and low-cost production capabilities. Core activities encompass large-scale copper mining, smelting, and refining through key assets like the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, alongside Mexico's strategic copper operations. The company excels in producing copper concentrates and cathodes, while also generating molybdenum and silver byproducts. Southern Copper sustains its competitive edge through significant copper reserves, supporting industrial copper supply and expansion projects. Emphasizing sustainability, the company adopts innovative mining practices and maintains robust supply chain management, positioning itself to leverage long-term trends in electric vehicles and base metals demand.

NYSE STOCK REPORT

PHOENIX, Tuesday, November 03 2026 - Ahead of this morning's market opening, Southern Copper Corporation closed lower the previous trading day. Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO), the NYSE's largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market cap, fell 2.2% during its previous trading session to close at $173.49.

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, renowned for its extensive copper mining operations and low-cost production capabilities. Core activities encompass large-scale copper mining, smelting, and refining through key assets like the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, alongside Mexico's strategic copper operations. The company excels in producing copper concentrates and cathodes, while also generating molybdenum and silver byproducts. Southern Copper sustains its competitive edge through significant copper reserves, supporting industrial copper supply and expansion projects. Emphasizing sustainability, the company adopts innovative mining practices and maintains robust supply chain management, positioning itself to leverage long-term trends in electric vehicles and base metals demand.

Southern Copper Corporation (NYSE:SCCO) is a leading integrated copper producer, renowned for its extensive copper mining operations and low-cost production capabilities. Core activities encompass large-scale copper mining, smelting, and refining through key assets like the Toquepala and Cuajone mines, alongside Mexico's strategic copper operations. The company excels in producing copper concentrates and cathodes, while also generating molybdenum and silver byproducts. Southern Copper sustains its competitive edge through significant copper reserves, supporting industrial copper supply and expansion projects. Emphasizing sustainability, the company adopts innovative mining practices and maintains robust supply chain management, positioning itself to leverage long-term trends in electric vehicles and base metals demand.

Company Profile

Southern Copper Corporation is an integrated copper producer operating mining units and metallurgical facilities in Mexico and Peru, with exploration activities in Argentina, Chile, Mexico and Peru. It is 88.9% owned by Grupo Mexico and listed in New York and Lima. Net sales reached $13,237.0 million in the first nine months of 2026, up 38.6% year over year, driven by higher prices across all products and modestly higher zinc sales volumes, partly offset by lower copper, molybdenum and silver volumes. Copper remains the principal revenue source, supplemented by molybdenum, zinc and silver by-products. Refined copper and rod output rose 10.1% year to date, while mined copper fell 2.9% on lower Peruvian ore grades.

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 4 nov (Reuters) - Analistas de grupos financieros y corredurías opinan sobre los mercados mexicanos y la economía. A continuación, un resumen de los reportes del 4 de noviembre. Las opiniones reflejadas no representan puntos de vista de Reuters.

PEPPERSTONE - Los mercados reevalúan las perspectivas políticas y económicas de Estados Unidos tras el control demócrata del Congreso. La renta variable cayó con fuerza al inicio de la sesión, especialmente el sector tecnológico, aunque los principales índices recuperaban terreno mientras los inversionistas evaluaban un Gobierno dividido.

* El peso mexicano MXN= se apreciaba un 0.9%, a 18.6505 unidades por dólar, frente a las 18.8208 unidades del precio de referencia de LSEG del martes.

BANORTE - Prevemos que la recuperación continúe. Una ruptura por debajo de 18.60 establecería una señal favorable. La siguiente resistencia se ubica en 18.50, mientras que el soporte está en 18.77. Recomendamos mantener posiciones.

ING - Los sondeos de opinión acertaron y los demócratas lograron una contundente victoria en las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos. Las tasas de interés de corto plazo estadounidenses y el dólar bajan ligeramente, mientras que los futuros accionarios recuperan parte de las pérdidas de entre 2% y 3% registradas durante la noche.
